A historic Swabian Alb knitwear mill — the classic multi-storey type with window grids on every floor. A conversion into 50 flats collapsed with 49 already sold, so expect scaffolding and partial works rather than a pristine ruin.

A textbook access route: insolvency proceedings opened in July 2026. An insolvency administrator controls the building, is named in the public register, and has every incentive to take a call.
next: Find the Insolvenzverwalter free on insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de. ⚠️ Sources disagree between Ebingen and Tailfingen — confirm the building before travelling.

name: Ehem. Hegau-Bodensee-Klinikum
status: City owns it, use concept pending
body:
A district hospital closed in June 2023 and formally handed to the city in June 2025. Full hospital volume — ward corridors, stairwells, multiple storeys.

As of July 2026 the city is drawing up a use concept before selling. The clearest institutional route on this list: a municipality that owns a building outright and is publicly mid-process has an interest in publicity.
next: Stadt Radolfzell Liegenschaftsamt or Stadtplanung, in writing.

name: Alte Klinik am Eichert
body:
A large hospital Altbau superseded by a new build — the press describes it as “verlassen, warm und ein kleines bisschen gruselig”, the heating still running. Demolition was decided in January 2026 at a cost of €28 million; at that price it will not vanish overnight, but the clock is running.

Journalists were let inside as recently as August 2025, so escorted access is evidently grantable.
next: The Klinikverbund or Landkreis Göppingen. Hard expiry — ask soon.

name: Schwarzwald-Parkhotel
body: Several listed buildings of the former Parkhotel stand empty. Windows smashed and the entrance forced, but rooms left furnished — beds still made, a Bible on a nightstand. Recently abandoned, so the fabric is intact and it has not yet been picked over.
next: The Gemeinde is the practical contact; the authorities describe themselves as largely powerless against an apparently absentee owner. That is a hint about who actually controls access.

name: Heilstätte Charlottenhöhe
body:
A 1907 tuberculosis sanatorium — a big institutional block in forest, and the region's best-known urbex target. ⚠️ Badly damaged by fire in October 2023 and cordoned off; described in July 2026 as a “vermüllte Brandruine” still rotting. The structure is no longer reliably whole.

Auctioned for €500,000 in 2025 to a buyer who then failed to pay. A fourth forced auction is expected.
next: Via the court rather than an owner — the Amtsgericht Calw auction department, and the Gemeinde. Position approximate.

name: Joffre-Areal / Joffre-Stallungen
body:
Fortress barracks of 1841, later a French garrison, empty since the withdrawal in the 1990s — including three listed Mannschaftsgebäude and the historic stables. Redevelopment into about 80 houses is permitted but stalled: July 2026 coverage runs under “Gestrüpp statt Bagger”, scrub instead of excavators, with the site going wild again.

⚠️ Baden-Airpark's control zone lies close to the south-west. Check before any outdoor line.
next: Stadt Rastatt plus the named developers. One project stalled after an investor died, so the ownership picture is worth untangling before you ask.

name: Hochrhein-Eggberg-Klinik
status: Four blocks, named owner, closing window
body:
A 1974 clinic in four building sections on a 10,600 m² site, empty for years with break-ins, ground-floor vandalism and fire damage. Classic layout: repeating window grids, long corridors, stacked ward floors.

A named property group bought it at forced auction in 2022 for €2 million and holds building permits for a seniors' campus. As of mid-2025 conversion was to start “next year” — so the derelict window is closing.
next: Contact the owning group directly. ⚠️ Newest evidence is 13 months old; verify before travelling.

name: Holtzmann-Areal (Papierfabrik)
body: A paper works founded in 1883 and wound down by 2006, with rusted machinery still in place — production halls plus a tall chimney flagged as dangerous. Notably unsecured: a 27-year-old was critically injured in a fall here and a neighbour publicly criticised the municipality for not fencing it.
next: Gemeinde Forbach, which is under public pressure over site safety — that cuts both ways: they may fence it, or may prefer a supervised visit to trespass. ⚠️ Evidence is 2.5 years old; it may have been secured since.

name: Schlosshotel Bühlerhöhe
body:
A 1912 grand hotel by Wilhelm Kreis at 770 m — three-storey main block, cylindrical central tower, two 27-metre wings. Vacant since August 2010.

⚠️ Important distinction: this is a maintained void, not a gutted bando. The owners were spending up to €100,000 a month on heating oil to prevent decay, and access to the building is reported as sealed. Calls for expropriation are growing.
next: No route in. The realistic intermediary is the preservation association that campaigns on the building. Ownership figures date from 2013–14.

name: Grand Hotel Römerbad
body:
A listed 68-room hotel, closed since early 2016 when the operator went insolvent mid-renovation. Partly renovated rather than gutted — 36 rooms were refurbished — so it is cleaner and less bando-like than the rest of this list. Rank it accordingly.

The Gemeinde has publicly examined whether expropriation is legally possible, which makes the municipality the lever rather than the absent owner.
next: Gemeinde Badenweiler. The expropriation debate means they are engaged and talking publicly.

name: Klinik Tettnang
body:
A hospital that ceased operations at the end of May 2026, 325 staff affected, future unresolved. Listed as a watch item: a just-closed hospital is intact rather than derelict.

⚠️ Tettnang sits close to Friedrichshafen airport. Assume a control zone. That is a legal blocker, not a nuisance.
next: Medizin Campus Bodensee or Stadt Tettnang — but settle the airspace question first, because it may make the rest moot.

name: Wanderer-Werke
body:
The former Wanderer bicycle, typewriter and motor works — one of the most significant industrial sites in Chemnitz. A 52 m-frontage administration and warehouse block, a 2,500 m² shed hall, heavily expanded up to the war: multi-storey brick with window grids around a large yard.

Confirmed flown. A named FPV video from April 2023 shot on a DJI Avata — one of the very few German bandos where a pilot published both the footage and the location.

⚠️ A major fire in March 2026 brought 60+ responders and hit the roof structure. Verify wholeness before travelling.
next: A private owner who has refused realistic offers, with expropriation publicly demanded. The city cannot compel action — route is the Chemnitz planning department. The site sits inside a ~100 ha redevelopment area.

name: Alter Schlachthof
body:
A former abattoir complex, derelict 33 years — “Natur holt sich alten halleschen Schlachthof zurück”.

Confirmed flown, twice. Two FPV videos from 2020 name it explicitly, both tagged Bando / Halle Saale / Schlachthof — including a cinematic edit.

⚠️ Go soon. A development plan for housing and retail was resolved in October 2025 and an investor announced in January 2026.
next: Stadt Halle planning department. The investor is not named in accessible reporting.

name: Ehemaliges SKET-Gelände
body:
The former heavy-machinery combine — a sprawling works. Parts of the wider site are active industry, so the derelict halls are pockets inside a live industrial park. Reconnoitre carefully.

Confirmed flown, twice — an FPV one-take from January 2022 and a revisit in March 2024, both naming the site.
next: A location-permission path demonstrably exists: the site has hosted art, culture and commercial photo shoots, including a magazine production. A cooperative was involved in development but is not named.

name: Erzgebirgsbad
body:
Disused indoor swimming baths — a hall building with pool basins and a substantial basement level, described in the press as “nasskalt, verlassen, totenstill”.

The best access route in the region. The town owns it outright and actively opens it: a rave and an art festival were held inside in October 2025, and four experts inspected it in April 2026.

⚠️ Window closing — the current news cycle is entirely about chasing renovation money.
next: Stadt Thalheim directly. A municipality that has already hosted a rave inside its derelict pool is not going to be shocked by a quad.

name: Mandaukaserne
body: A huge castle-like 19th-century barracks — the press calls it an “XXL-Immobilie mit hunderten Zimmern” and a “burgartiges Riesendenkmal”. Long-corridor, repeated-window-bay geometry at real scale.
next: Excellent: an active friends' association runs a volunteer circle and lighting events, and a dentist was permitted to plan a practice inside part of the building. Approach the association, not the owner.

name: Kulturpalast „Wilhelm Pieck“
body:
Neoclassical monumental architecture from 1953 — a 1,000-seat main auditorium, restaurant, smaller stages and over 240 rooms. Closed 1996 and derelict since; the cellar was filled with concrete after contaminated groundwater ingress. Heritage-protected, and a 2017 demolition application was refused.

A €20m musical conversion collapsed, so it stays derelict.
next: A private owner who inherited it from the previous investor. No institutional route.

name: Kulturpalast Unterwellenborn
body:
Opened 1955, listed since 1987. A 700-seat theatre with a 360 m² stage, a music salon for 200, a foyer with gallery for 320, a small hall and a café. Mosaics of the five muses, marble floors, travertine stairs, more than fifty distinct light fittings.

⚠️ Empty since 1990 with severe water ingress from failed roofing, heavy theft, and a documented risk of ceiling collapse in the theatre hall.
next: A named property company in Kronach owns it, and the municipality is engaged — the mayor is named in coverage.

name: Papierfabrik Golzern
body:
A paper mill on the Mulde abandoned in July 2013 after the flood — 60 staff and 30,000 t a year before closure. Listed as one comprehensive monument: a three-storey rubble-stone production building with its original timber staircase and cast-iron columns in the former turbine hall, a second three-storey block, a 1910 Kalandersaal with segment-arched windows, a 1927 clinker turbine house and an 1880s boiler house.

Note: the owner-friendly Alte Spitzenfabrik is 8 km away.
next: The town owned it and council approved sale in October 2023; a Leipzig architecture practice publicly bid to revive it. Buyer not named — the town building department is the route.

name: Sophienheilstätte
body:
Founded 1898, raised to 200 beds in 1911 — main building plus pavilions, woodland rest halls, treatment rooms, laboratories and an X-ray wing, in forest above the Ilm valley. Vacant since 1994 with progressive decay.

The interior is already licensed commercially: a Halloween event was staged there and a ZDF drama filmed there. A location manager and an event operator both hold working access.
next: The owning group has invested nothing since 2002 — so go via the people who already get in: the location manager or the event operator.

name: Böllberger Mühle
body:
A large multi-storey brick mill — a “Backsteinkoloss” on the Saale bank.

A film production shot there in January 2026, which confirms it is standing and enterable this year and proves a location-permission route exists. The coordinate was independently cross-validated by two separate lookups.
next: Via the film-location route rather than the owner. Whoever cleared that shoot can clear another.

name: Kulturhaus Krumpa
body:
The large-hall Kulturhaus typology — the same building class as Bitterfeld and Unterwellenborn. Storey count and dimensions not yet established.

The best kind of access route: a forced auction at the Amtsgericht Merseburg. Auction files are public and the valuation report normally carries floor plans, storey counts and interior photographs — so you can answer the volume question before you drive.
next: The auction court. Request the Verkehrswertgutachten; it is public and it will tell you whether the hall is worth the trip.

name: Heilstätte Carolagrün
body:
A main complex of 1899–1900, a neo-Gothic timber chapel of 1906 later converted to a sports hall, a 1907 children's wing, a separate 40-bed children's home of 1913, and three multi-storey residential blocks from the 1970s. Heritage-protected, empty since 2000.

⚠️ No recent press exists at all — treat the condition as unverified since about 2019.
next: A foreign investor bought it in 2004 and it deteriorated markedly afterwards. No named contact — that is the weak point here.

name: Sanatorium Schwarzeck
body:
A lung sanatorium of 1893 that became a Luftwaffe engineering school and then an SED party school. The site runs to about 50 hectares: a five-storey “Camburger Bau”, a massive main building, a hall building and a Swiss house. Vacant since 2004; restoration is costed at around €20m.

Interiors are being entered — a torchlight walkthrough was reported in 2025.

⚠️ Ownership is actively contested in court, and the site is politically sensitive after a failed purchase by a political party was blocked by a judge.
next: No clean route while ownership is in litigation.

name: Buntpapierfabrik
body:
A multi-storey brick paper-mill complex that hosted an urban-art festival in 2021 — so the interior volumes are documented and photogenic, with murals still in place as of mid-2025.

⚠️ It was sealed after the festival: “Jetzt wird abgeschlossen”.
next: The festival organising team negotiated access in 2021 and is the obvious intermediary; otherwise the town. No owner named in accessible reporting.

name: Kraftwerk Hirschfelde
body: Surviving fabric includes the machine house of Works II from 1918/1929, the administration building, main warehouse, a pump station, and the kitchen and dining hall — clinker brick, 1921 to the 1950s. The power-plant museum closed in June 2017 because of structural deterioration and the collections were dispersed.
next: Clear and named: the energy company owns it and regained the machine house in 2018. A foundation also exists, now doing digital archiving.

name: Ehem. Kneipp-Sanatorium Löhma
body:
Built in 1965 by converting worker accommodation from the nearby pumped-storage scheme, then a gastro-intestinal spa clinic. Four structures — social building, cultural building, connecting block and nursing quarters. Empty since 1993, over thirty years. Cultural monument.

⚠️ Sold to a developer in late 2021, but a later headline reports an investor withdrawing, so the sale may not have stuck.
next: The state development company held it for ~25 years before selling. Start there or with the district — the ownership question needs settling first.

name: Ehemalige JVA Gera
body:
A prison closed in October 2017 — cell blocks, long corridors, multi-storey with window grids. On paper that is strong FPV geometry. Offered for sale in 2019 at €300,000 with reported strong interest.

⚠️ Newest verifiable evidence is October 2021. Condition and current ownership are unconfirmed.
next: Sold by the state; part of the site reverted to the previous owner in 2021. Current buyer not established — try the state property management or the city.

name: Alte Malzfabrik (”roter Riese”)
body:
A large brick malt factory on the Saale.

⚠️ Mixed signals: a new investor took over an adjacent housing project in October 2024, but the weighbridge house of the neighbouring “Kleine Malzfabrik” was demolished in October 2023 for slip risk. Confirm what actually stands before going.
next: The town has been involved. Worth a call to establish which buildings survive.

name: Malzfabrik Niedersedlitz
body:
A malt works in three build phases from 1873 to 1916, production ceased 1991. The city has secured it and retail, office and housing plans exist, but nothing has started — “Wieder nichts: Kein Bagger in Sicht”.

⚠️ Serious caution. Fires in 2020, 2022, twice in January 2025 and an arson in February 2025, plus a partial demolition in 2022 for acute collapse risk. It fails the “structurally whole” test in parts. Listed for completeness, not recommended.
next: Stadt Dresden. Realistically this is a record rather than an opportunity.

name: Kurhäuser Bad Reiboldsgrün
body:
A former Saxon lung-sanatorium estate of about 66 hectares — treatment buildings, patient accommodation, laundry, power house and medical residences. Most of the Kurhäuser have been empty since the operator left in the late 1990s.

⚠️ Partly redeveloped: clinic buildings were modernised and a forestry training centre opened on the site in 2023. Only some buildings remain empty — confirm which before travelling.
next: Historically a sanatorium association, later a regional hospital. Needs untangling.

name: Schloss Rodberg
body:
Despite the name this is a former sanatorium, not a castle ruin — built 1911, opened 1912. The main building is four storeys with a central risalit and two corner towers, in forest near the Ilm. Empty and decaying since 2000, with a fire in 2015. Cultural monument since 1999.

⚠️ Most recent verifiable evidence is 2021 — over three years old. Re-check before travelling.
next: Privately owned since 1996, owner not named. Sale talks with a citizens' initiative were reported around 2015. No usable contact.

name: Kraftwerk Vockerode
body:
A former lignite and gas-turbine power station on the Elbe, decommissioned 1994. The four 140 m chimneys were blown in 2001 and the gas-turbine stacks in 2013, but the machine halls remain.

⚠️ It sits inside both the Mittelelbe biosphere reserve and a UNESCO garden-realm site, so drone flight is legally restricted under nature-protection provisions. Listed so you can rule it out deliberately rather than discover it on arrival.
next: None established, and the airspace question settles it anyway.

name: Jüterbog II Kaserne
body:
About 30 hectares of listed barracks, derelict for years. Bought in 2018 by a property group that turned out to be fraudulent and insolvent; no investment was ever made.

The strongest access route in the region: the insolvency administrator plans a sale in 2026. That is a named professional with a legal duty to realise the asset — and every reason to take a call.

The big nature reserve nearby covers the open heath, not the urban blocks — but verify the parcel line.
next: Write to the insolvency administrator. ⚠️ Condition detail dates to 2018; confirm what stands.

name: Haus der Offiziere / Waldstadt Wünsdorf
body:
A six-building neo-baroque ensemble of 1914–16 totalling about 23,000 m² of floor space — main hall, swimming hall, theatre and gymnasium, commandant's residence. Vacant since 1994, listed, and must be sold as one complex.

⚠️ The site is permanently guarded. Go through the development company, not over a fence.
next: The development company that markets it publishes a named contact and phone number — it is actively seeking investors, confirmed October 2025.

name: Flugplatz Sperenberg
body:
A 2,400-hectare ex-Soviet airfield, owned by the state of Brandenburg since 2009. “Sämtliche Gebäude und Installationen sind dem Verfall preisgegeben” — the largest structure is a maintenance hangar, plus bunkers and the former guesthouse.

Not on the Bundeswehr reactivation list; only a separate fuel-depot parcel is.
next: A military-museum association runs area tours, and the mayor is named in coverage — a plausible ask route. ⚠️ Unexploded ordnance clearance was costed at €11.3m, though that figure is from 2007.

name: Ehemalige Molkerei
body:
A disused dairy, empty for decades, with roof surfaces already collapsed and “viele Räumlichkeiten zum Erkunden”. A construction fence went up recently.

The best access route in this survey: the municipality has owned the site since mid-2025 and the mayor is on record. A municipal owner is far easier than an insolvency estate.
next: The Gemeinde directly. ⚠️ Not mapped in OSM, so the footprint is unverified — it is on the B103 at the Bad Stuer turn-off, and the pin is village-centre approximate.

name: ”Russen-Kaserne” Berliner Straße
body:
About 37,000 m² with four barracks buildings “der Witterung preisgegeben” — 1930s fabric, substance described as “grundsolide” despite a failed roof.

⚠️ By July 2026 the front building had been gutted for refugee housing with work paused pending district approval; the rear blocks still have no usage plan. That is the window.

Distinct from the active Uckermark-Kaserne elsewhere in town.
next: The district-owned development company — its managing director and site manager are both named in coverage, as is the Landrätin. Pin is road-level, not building-precise.

name: Ehem. Kurhotel Zippendorf
body:
A listed hotel of 1910, empty for years — broken panes, crumbling render, graffiti. A structural report was filed in January 2026 on whether preservation is economically reasonable, and the city insists on renovation rather than demolition.

⚠️ Lakeside caution: adjacent meadows are a landscape protection area and two nearby islands are full nature reserves, where recreational flight is barred outright.
next: The owning company and its managing director are both named, as is the city building commissioner. A clean, fully-named counterparty.

name: Flugplatz Pütnitz
body:
Five large 1935 Wehrmacht hangars plus a Werfthalle survive; the tower is a ruin.

Demolition was stopped by a court in October 2025 over bat roosts, and conservationists forced a further halt in March 2026. So the structures stand and are legally protected from removal — but that same protection cuts against anyone entering.

A €400m holiday-village conversion targets no opening before 2029.
next: The town development company, or the technical association that operates the museum halls. ⚠️ The Bodden surroundings are very likely Natura 2000 — verify before flying.

name: Heilanstalten Hohenlychen
body:
About 16 hectares and 47 buildings by the mid-1920s. Partly converted — nine buildings became flats and holiday apartments with a bistro, around 40% of the listed fabric renovated — but the majority of the complex still stands empty, with occasional guided tours.

⚠️ Residents live on site. This is not unobserved ground.
next: The family running the conversion project is named and continues to develop it. In a nature park — check the overlay.

name: Kaserne Fünfeichen
body:
The Bundeswehr left in 2015, brief refugee use followed in 2015/16, and it has been empty since. A 400-place refugee facility was floated in 2024 and stopped by the city that December.

A competing conversion by a named investor is running under a development plan over about 8.8 hectares. Not on the reactivation list.
next: The investor company, or the city planner named in the press. Protection status unchecked.

name: Neues Lager / Standortlazarett
body: A Prussian garrison from 1889 that served as a military hospital under the Wehrmacht and then Soviet forces until the early 1990s, unused since. Numerous Kaiserzeit military buildings survive; the hospital and granary are listed. About 80,000 m², mostly held by a company owned by the state of Brandenburg.
next: That company's name is the missing piece — the local paper is paywalled and blocks automated access. Worth one phone call to the state property arm.

name: Papierfabrik Neu Kaliß
body:
Production ended on 31 March 2026 after the owner approached around 170 investors without finding a buyer: “Was mit diesen Hallen geschieht, kann jetzt noch nicht gesagt werden.” Large modern paper halls, still secured.

Too recent to be derelict — this is a watch item. Revisit in a year.
next: The corporate owner, or the Landrat who is named in coverage. ⚠️ The OSM name may denote the older adjacent works, so the footprint is unconfirmed.

name: Malzfabrik ”Wismaria”
body:
An 1898 maltworks, once the region's second largest — multi-storey brick with ventilation towers, by the mill pond. Empty since 1992 and listed.

⚠️ Partly collapsed, so it fails the structurally-whole test in places.
next: An investor bought it in 2019, secured a positive planning opinion, then went insolvent in 2023; neither the investor nor the administrator could be recovered. Fall back to the city building department.

name: Ehem. Lehrlingswohnheim
body:
An empty high-rise plus complex — genuinely large. But ⚠️ twelve fires in 2026 alone, repeated rescues, heavy vandalism. The owner is insolvent and the object is in forced auction with no date set, while the city is erecting a fence with video surveillance at its own cost.

The worst access prospect in this region: police, fire service and cameras, in a residential district.
next: The city building authority, or the court for the auction file. Realistically a record rather than an opportunity.

name: Artilleriekaserne Eggesin-Karpin
body:
Described as “eine der größten Kasernen der DDR”, auctioned in 2019.

⚠️ No source after 2019 on the buyer, the condition, or whether it still stands. Phone before travelling. And the adjacent training area is active Bundeswehr — do not stray.
next: The local Amt, which offers form-only contact. Position is approximate — an Ortsteil centroid, not the barracks.

name: NVA-Kaserne Goldberg/Damerow
body:
A tank regiment disbanded in 1991; part of the site became a commercial technology park but the accommodation blocks have stood empty since. Tagged military=abandoned in OpenStreetMap.

⚠️ The last datable evidence is a 2017 photograph — no press at all from 2023 onwards. Verify first.
next: None established.

name: Flugplatz Brand-Briesen (remainder)
body:
The main hangar is now a tropical resort and is excluded — but the base held around 5,000 soldiers, and hardened aircraft shelters, the 1974 tower and fuel and ammunition facilities are documented, with derelict structures reported beyond the resort.

⚠️ Ownership, condition and protection status could not be established at all. A genuine lead with no verification behind it.
next: None established. Treat as reconnaissance, not a plan.

name: Helios Seehospital Sahlenburg
body:
A former seaside hospital, used until September 2023 as a refugee arrival centre and completely empty since — a multi-building clinic campus with ward blocks and connecting corridors, visibly deteriorating.

⚠️ Sahlenburg sits against the Wattenmeer national park boundary, where recreational flight is barred. Check the exact line before flying.
next: Unusually open: the owner runs a public page for the site inviting reports of vandalism and defects — a rare direct channel to a corporate owner.

name: Kraftwerk Farge
body:
A 350 MW hard-coal station on the Weser, taken off the grid in April 2024. Full power-station envelope — boiler house, turbine hall, bunker structures.

The owner plans Germany's largest battery storage on the site, but permitting must run first and only then partial demolition. That is the window, and it is closing.

⚠️ Bunker Valentin is about 1 km away and is a formal memorial — treat that airspace as off-limits.
next: The owning power group, with the city economic development body as secondary channel.

name: Elisabeth-Krankenhaus Thuine
body: A full hospital closed in February 2025 following insolvency, standing empty while a feasibility study runs. Recent closure means intact fabric — ward corridors and stairwells still sound rather than stripped.
next: The strongest formal route in the region: the insolvency administration is a named party, and the district commissioned the reuse study.

name: Regio Klinikum Wedel
body:
Closed in 2020 and largely empty since — substantial enough to have served as the filming location for an ARD Polizeiruf 110. ⚠️ Parts are still in use: the city rents the former nurses' home as emergency accommodation.

⚠️ Directly under the Hamburg control zone and beside the Elbe approach. The most airspace-constrained site in the region.
next: The city holds a standing tenancy with the named owner and published the arrangement — ask the city first. But settle the airspace question before anything else.

name: Ehem. Krankenhaus Priwall
body:
Empty since 2005. ⚠️ Three of the buildings were demolished from March onward; roughly two century-old buildings remain.

The city resolved in February 2026 to sell to the highest bidder — about 10,000 m², minimum bid €3.26m, with the express condition that the remaining buildings need not be preserved.
next: An unusually well-documented public route: the city property management, with the sale file in the council information system. Verify the two buildings still stand.

name: Ehem. Sanatorium Hängebargshorst
body:
An orthopaedic and cardiovascular rehabilitation clinic closed in 2006 — a multi-storey block in parkland by the lakes. Reported as sealed, all entrances locked or boarded: good for structural integrity, bad for entry.

⚠️ Evidence is around five years old. Verify before travelling.
next: None identified. No current owner surfaced — the municipal building department is the place to start.

name: Zuckerfabrik Obernjesa
body:
The sugar-factory seam paying off: production has ceased and two large sugar silos remain as the village landmark, explicitly recorded as no longer in use. The complex is a listed monument and carries a disused-works tag.

⚠️ The silos and disuse are confirmed; the interior state of the halls is not.
next: The municipality references the factory in its own pages, and the district heritage authority is involved because of the listing.

name: Alte Müllverbrennungsanlage
body:
A waste incineration plant abandoned at the end of the 1980s which, according to explorer accounts, may never have gone into operation at all. Plant structure with boiler-hall volume, mapped as a ruin.

⚠️ Not the active incinerator, which is in the same district. Two plants, one district — confirm you have the right one.
next: None identified — the designing firm has been dissolved, which is exactly why ownership is murky. City property department is the first call.

name: Roswitha-Klinik (former)
body:
A rehabilitation clinic for psychotherapy, empty since the 2017 insolvency of its operator, with plants growing up the façade.

⚠️ A working clinic of almost the same name operates 500 m away — do not fly that one. Police reports indicate repeated incidents on the derelict site, so expect scrutiny.
next: Blocked: the former operator confirmed the sale but would not name the buyer. The town building department is the only lead.

name: Klinik Veerßen
body:
A former clinic standing empty with investor plans reported as stalled. ⚠️ The building has burned more than once — the brigade was called to a fully involved fire at 01:34, the headline using “wieder”.

Fire damage means structural integrity is doubtful; this may no longer meet the structurally-whole bar.
next: The town and district are handling reuse; investor names were not published.

name: Ehemalige JVA Braunschweig
body:
A disused prison — and prisons are strong FPV architecture: cell galleries, long straight landings, stairwell voids.

⚠️ Mapping data only, condition unverified. City-centre location means observers.
next: A former prison would sit with the state justice ministry or state building management.

name: Altenzentrum Neumühlen-Dietrichsdorf
body:
Recorded with seven storeys and a disused social-facility tag. Seven floors with a repeating window grid is exactly the vertical freestyle profile, on the Kiel east bank near the Schwentine mouth.

⚠️ Mapping data only — unverified.
next: Not identified. The city is the starting point.

name: Ehemalige Ziegelei Sunder
body:
A disused brickworks — kiln halls and drying sheds give good volume, and the rural setting means low observation.

⚠️ Mapping data only. Whether the buildings survive at all is unknown.
next: Not identified.

name: Diabas-Werke Langelsheim
body:
An abandoned hard-stone processing works. These carry tall crushing and screening structures with internal steelwork — good vertical geometry.

⚠️ Mapping data only, unverified.
next: Not identified.

name: U-Boot-Bunker Fink II
body:
A wartime submarine bunker — massive concrete, but heavily demolished post-war, so expect a partial structure rather than an intact pen.

⚠️ Hamburg CTR plus the immediate proximity of the Airbus Finkenwerder runway makes this effectively unflyable. Listed for completeness, not recommendation.
next: None. The airspace settles it.

name: Fliegerhorst Penzing / ”Area61”
status: 270 ha — and they want film crews
body:
A former Luftwaffe base of roughly 270 hectares with retained historic hangars and barrack blocks under partial listing, bought from the federal agency for €40 million by a joint authority of the two local councils, completed June 2026.

The best-documented access route in the survey: the development plan explicitly designates a “Sondergebiet Filmkulisse” — a film-set special zone — and the operator's stated aims include innovative film production. A public body that actively wants creative users on site.

⚠️ It was on the Bundeswehr reactivation radar in October 2025 and released that December, but a partial military lease for accommodation may still be open. Confirm current status.
next: The joint authority running the site publishes an address and website. Approach as a film production — that is the door they have already opened.

name: Ehemalige Porzellanfabrik Arzberg
body:
A ruined porcelain works “spanning thousands of square metres”, moss- and fern-covered ceilings, machinery still in place — the plant employed around 600 people at its peak, on a site of about 11.4 hectares.

The strongest route in Franconia: three commercial operators sell access. A camera manufacturer runs photo workshops there, and two photo-tour companies sell tickets — one at €78. Any of them can put you inside legally.
next: Book through one of the photo-tour operators. ⚠️ Position approximate, and confirm which building the tours use — part of the wider site was redeveloped around 2021.

name: Alte Spinnerei Mainleus
body:
A large multi-building cotton-spinning works, abandoned since the dye house closed in 2013. A distinct boiler house is used for cultural events while the bulk stands empty.

Precedent exists: artists were given organised access in 2025, and the municipality is running the reuse project.

⚠️ Do not confuse with the “Alte Spinnerei am Bahnhof” in Kulmbach town, which is converted and in use.
next: The municipality runs the project and licenses the site for festivals; the festival organisers are a second route.

name: Ehem. Schlachthof ”Ochsenkathedrale”
body:
A former municipal slaughterhouse, listed, locally famous as the “Ochsenkathedrale” — a nickname that tells you about the single big hall volume. A stalled multi-million renovation has left the city publicly frustrated with the owner.

A documentary was filmed there in 2025, which proves filming access is grantable. ⚠️ Some ancillary demolition happened in 2023, so not every structure survives.
next: Two named, reachable parties in open dispute over deadlines: the developer group and the town hall. Disputes make people talk.

name: Hotel Rixen
body:
A gutted hotel block of six storeys with a basement level — the tallest single volume in the Bavarian survey and a genuine stacked-floor interior.

Renovation has been abandoned in favour of a sale, reported March 2026.
next: An estate agent will be attached to the disposal. That is the way in — agents want the building seen.

name: Leopoldkaserne
body: A disused barracks complex with listed buildings, empty and awaiting conversion into a new city quarter — substantial masonry blocks with regular floor plans. Conversion is starting at the edges but the bulk is still empty.
next: A municipal development company bought the site in August 2024. A named public company with a development mandate is an unusually approachable owner.

name: Maxhütte
body:
Bavaria's last conventional blast-furnace steelworks, up to 9,000 employees at peak, finally insolvent after about 150 years. An enormous rusting complex; the blast furnace itself is preserved as a monument and hosts events.

⚠️ Be careful. Two regional outlets reported in January 2025 that lost-place visitors were caught and prosecuted.
next: Via the town, which co-runs events at the furnace — permitted access demonstrably happens. Do not improvise here.

name: Conn Barracks
body:
A former US Army airfield-and-barracks complex of roughly 200 hectares, in municipal hands since December 2025. Explicitly not on the Bundeswehr reactivation freeze, so no military reversion risk.

⚠️ Move fast. Earmarked for an AI gigafactory and commercial park with planning law targeted for summer 2026; large-scale clearance is imminent. Part of the wider area hosts occupied refugee accommodation which must be avoided.
next: The joint authority of town and district that bought it; the district runs the development plan process. Position approximate.

name: Rotkreuzklinik Lindenberg
body:
A full district hospital closed and liquidated after insolvency in mid-2024, inpatient care ending that July. A complete multi-storey clinical building with wards, corridors and stairwells intact — empty but not yet gutted.

As of February 2026 three concrete reuse ideas were on the table.
next: A liquidation means an administrator is on record — that is your named counterparty. The town is handling the reuse debate.

name: Theresienklinik
body:
A former hospital of a religious congregation, closed in January 2025 when another operator took over inpatient work. A substantial city-centre clinical building; the question of what happens to the rooms was still open in mid-2025.

⚠️ Dense historic city centre — overflight of an inhabited Altstadt block is a separate legal problem from access.
next: Both the retreating congregation and the incoming operator are named, institutional and contactable.

name: KunstFabrik / Schoedel-Hallen
body: Former textile works — large empty factory halls. One 2025 exhibition alone used over 320 m² and drew around 30 artists across a two-day festival, now in its second annual edition. Raw industrial volume, temporarily fitted for events and otherwise empty.
next: The arts association that runs the programme is named and locally based. Position approximate.

name: Ehem. Krankenhaus Hersbruck
body:
A district hospital closed in June 2019 after a contested decision.

⚠️ Evidence is over three years old and current condition is unverified — and a neighbouring clinic is still trading, so parts of the campus are live.
next: The operating company is still recorded as a named, contactable entity — which is the main reason this stays on the list.

name: Ehemalige Porzellanfabrik Tettau
body:
One of Bavaria's oldest porcelain makers, founded 1794, production ceased in 2019. Local press called the empty plant a “Koloss” and a problem for the town. Largely abandoned buildings, some collapsed ceilings, security measures, parts privately leased.

⚠️ Nothing since 2021. Partial collapse is reported. Verify it still stands before committing a trip.
next: The municipality is the party publicly wrestling with it; no owner or administrator was named. Position approximate.

name: Goodyear-Werk Fulda
body:
The largest object in the survey area. A tyre plant that ran 125 years with about 1,000 staff; production ended in September 2025. A multi-hall production complex plus multi-storey ancillary buildings on a near-inner-city site.

Broadcasters visited in July 2026 — “So sieht das verlassene Goodyear-Werk heute aus” and “Lost-Place-Vibes” — so it was standing, gutted and genuinely empty a month ago.

⚠️ Time-critical: the development plan runs to 2028 and demolition is explicitly on the table.
next: The city bought it in July 2026 for €16.2m and ran its first public site tour that same month — a live municipal contact and a precedent for admitting visitors. Go via the city planning office.

name: Burger Hütte / JUNO-Werk
body:
An iron foundry founded in 1727, later Germany's JUNO cooker and enamelware works, then Buderus, then Electrolux — about 2,000 workers at its 1960s peak. Production moved away in 2019.

Mapping still carries a dozen large halls: 236×120 m, 180×148 m, 163×133 m, 140×112 m, 88×87 m, plus office blocks. The biggest single run of interior volume in the entire national survey.

⚠️ Mixed live/dead campus — parts are re-let to small firms, and no press since 2019 confirms which halls are empty. Scout tenancy before committing.
next: The town economic development office, a named local developer, and the local industrial museum for contacts. Not monument-listed.

name: Ehem. Kurklinik ”Sonnenhof”
body:
A former sanatorium in woodland above the village — a 1,895 m² main building plus a separate 689 m² doctors' villa, so a genuine two-building complex. Derelict well over a decade; a forced auction collapsed for the second time in 2019 and a children's-hotel plan never happened.

⚠️ It burned in May 2026 in a major fire-service callout. No demolition reported in the three months since — assume floor damage in at least one wing.

The most-filmed site in the region for urbex, with several named walkthrough videos. Documented but never flown.
next: The failed-auction file at the district court names the current owner; the municipality holds the fire and demolition orders.

name: Klinik Balzerborn
body:
A multi-building rehabilitation complex on the hillside — a 3,228 m² main block and about 9,400 m² across 14 structures within 200 m. Long ward corridors, multiple storeys, regular window grids.

Ordered shut by the district in 2023 after hygiene failures, stopped admitting patients that October, insolvent with an administrator appointed July 2024. No reuse or demolition reported since.
next: The insolvency administrator is named in local press and the court file is public — a clean professional counterparty.

name: Helios Klinik Oberwald
body:
A hospital closed in May 2025, with inpatients gone a year earlier. The November 2025 headline is literally “Oberwaldklinik verwaist und versiegelt”, and in March 2026 the press was still asking what happens to the building — nine months empty with no successor use agreed.

⚠️ Do not confuse with the clinic at Ilbeshausen-Hochwaldhausen, which is fully operating.
next: The closing operator owns it; the municipality and district are both publicly pressing for a new use, which is a receptive posture.

name: Neues Landhotel Vogelsberg
body:
A large Kneipp-era hotel block, empty over a decade and locally known as the “Geisterhotel” — press in 2019 reported guest data still lying loose inside. It burned in January 2025; fire extent is unconfirmed, so treat structural wholeness as unverified until you see it.

The ownership is the story: the building is in Chinese ownership and the local SPD publicly demanded the embassy be involved because the owner is unreachable.
next: The town and district building authorities have chased the owner for years and hold the file. Nobody is coming to stop you, which is why this is the one open entry here.

name: Ringlokschuppen Dillenburg
body:
A 16-stall roundhouse from the 1915 expansion, later extended toward 25, plus workshops, the running office and a massive concrete coaling plant, on 16,700 m². The last federal depot to run class 94.5 steam. German Wikipedia says the buildings were left “dem Zerfall überlassen”.

Radial roundhouse bays are close to ideal FPV geometry — every line converges on the turntable.
next: The best permission prospect in the survey: the town bought it from the railway at auction in December 2019 for €155,000. A municipal owner, not an absent investor. ⚠️ Evidence is three years old and the roofs badly need work.

name: Kurbad-Therme Bad Hersfeld
body:
A full thermal-bath hall in the Kurpark — pool halls give exactly the clear-span volume and glass that freestyle wants. Shut in September 2022 during the energy crisis and declared permanently closed in March 2023.

Still shut as of April 2026: negotiations with a hotel operator collapsed and a would-be buyer is now building his own pool instead. Nearly four years dark with no successor.
next: The town owns it and is the party negotiating its future. A municipal building with a failed sale is an unusually good ask target.

name: Klinik Waldhof Elgershausen
body:
Founded 1900 as a TB Heilstätte and grown into one of the region's main lung clinics. The lung department moved to Gießen in March 2021, emptying the multi-storey ward block — textbook sanatorium form, long corridors, regular window grid.

The wider 18-hectare, 11-building campus is being revived as a community with a café and events, but the big clinic building is the one nobody has found a use for.
next: The most askable owner on the list: a citizens' foundation holds the site, and the village association publishes a contact email outright. The mayor sits on the board.

name: Schoeller Electronics
body:
A former global-player printed-circuit-board maker; production wound up in January 2021 after insolvency. A real multi-hall electronics works — clean-room bays and long production halls — on the edge of a small town.

Local press ran it as “Suche nach Lösungen für ‘Lost Place' in Wetter”, with the district chief and mayor publicly brainstorming uses.
next: Both the town and the district have gone public looking for a solution — that is an invitation. The insolvency administrator is the other route. ⚠️ Verify it has not been sold since 2024.

name: Hütt-Brauerei
body:
A 270-year-old brewery that stopped brewing in late 2025 for lack of a successor. The brand, recipes and supply contracts went to a Westphalian brewery, so the site keeps nothing — brewhouse, fermentation cellars, bottling hall and tank farm remain.

Classic brewery volume, dark less than a year: the best possible window before stripping.
next: The owning family via the town. The buyer took only the brand, not the property, so they can point you at the seller.

name: Cartonia Wellpappen
body:
A corrugated-board plant closed in May 2025 with 75 employees. One big production hall plus high-bay storage, and it went dark barely a year ago so the fabric should be unstripped.

A municipality-funded acquisition of about €5m was reported in January 2026.

⚠️ Check the control zone — the nearby airport has blocked wind turbines in this municipality.
next: The municipality, since the purchase figure is a municipal budget line. Mayor and building office.

name: AquaSalis-Therme
body:
A brine and thermal bath declared permanently closed in 2017 because the structural damage was too great to repair — exactly the state that leaves a whole shell with nothing worth salvaging inside.

The replacement still is not built: the municipality imposed a moratorium in 2023 over cost explosion and was still debating lifting it in late 2024. Nine years empty.
next: The municipality owns it and is running the moratorium debate; the spa administration is named.

name: Sportbad Baunatal
body:
A 2,105 m² pool hall with a 3,193 m² adjoining public building and a 3,558 m² sports hall alongside — a former competition pool the press calls an ex-“Olympia-Schmiede”. Drained basin, big clear span.

The council voted for demolition in 2023 but never carried it out; as of March 2026 the town is running an investor and ideas competition, so it stands.
next: The town owns it and the ideas competition is a named public process — a genuine ask rather than a trespass.

name: Alte Textilfabrik Weyhers
body:
A genuine old textile mill with the window-grid façades you want. Demolition was actively stopped in 2022 and conversion concepts exist — 22 flats, a park, a roof terrace — but development “scheint zu stagnieren” as of late 2025 and was still at the next-steps stage in January 2026.

Preserved, unconverted, stalled: the ideal window.
next: The housing cooperative driving the conversion, via the municipality — the mayor is quoted pushing it. ⚠️ Position approximate; the building would not geocode by name.

name: Ringlokschuppen Bw Eschwege West
body:
A semicircular railway engine shed. Single-storey, but the radial bay volume flies well.

The station went to auction in 2017; in April 2022 a private buyer announced he would restore the roundhouse, and nothing has been reported since — so either still shell-derelict or partly worked on.
next: The named private purchaser, the district court auction record, or the town building office. ⚠️ Over three years old — verify.

name: Wicker Klinik am Homberg
body:
Closed by its operator group in October 2024, with dozens of jobs lost; the group has since consolidated its specialisms elsewhere and the clinic's own domain now redirects to the group site — consistent with a fully retired property.

A detailed sweep of the spa town found this is the only large empty clinic left — everything else is demolished or operating.
next: A named private owner that has publicly retired the asset, plus the town building office. ⚠️ Position approximate — the clinic is no longer in any gazetteer.

name: Großkraftwerk Main-Weser
body:
A lignite power station in service 1923–1991 — and crucially, the designed buildings were deliberately kept when the plant was dismantled. Only chimneys and cooling towers came down, leaving a monumental 1920s turbine and boiler hall complex intact.

Used privately for markets, a disco and a museum, but the flea markets ended in 2024, so the halls are now largely without a use.

⚠️ The surrounding estate hosts active firms and the old switchyard is a live 380 kV substation — stay well clear of that.
next: The private investor named in coverage as seeking partners, plus the town. A permission site, not a derelict one.

name: Gießerei Lollar
body:
Descendant of an 1854 ironworks, the industrial spine of the town on a narrow strip between the Lahn and the railway. Closure was announced in September 2025 and the foundry shut at year-end with 230 jobs lost; by January 2026 the investor search was reported as going badly.

⚠️ A major manufacturer still runs about 1,000 staff on the adjoining part of the same strip. Manned perimeter.
next: The owning investment group, the union, and the state economics ministry are all engaged — but the live neighbour makes this permission-only.

name: DAG-Werk Allendorf (Herrenwald)
body:
Two explosives works of about 420 hectares each, together the largest munitions site in wartime Europe — 413 buildings in one works alone. Post-war demolition took 97 production buildings, but the rest survived and the camouflage berms were stripped, so what remains are above-ground concrete halls, not buried bunkers.

⚠️ Read this before going. An active rapid-forces barracks is about 2 km east. In October 2025 local press ran “Bei Drohnenflügen über Stadtallendorfer Kasernen drohen Strafen” and “Drohnenflug über Kaserne kostet Tausende Euro Strafe”. People have been fined thousands of euros here within the last year. Keep well west of the barracks line.
next: The town museum, in the former works head office, runs guided site walks — that is the correct front door. The forestry authority holds the woodland parcels.

name: Parkhotel + Bürgerhaus Biedenkopf
body:
Two adjacent buildings, both shut since 2020.

⚠️ Window closing fast: the town sold them to an investor on 30 May 2026 for renovation, so works will start.
next: The town sold them and can name the purchaser. Go now or not at all.

name: Buderus Edelstahl
body:
Hessen's last steelworks; the last working day was 31 October 2025 with around 470 jobs lost. The melt shop is dead but the campus is not empty — the buyer of the forging divisions is actively forging there in 2026, and the land itself is contested between property investors.

⚠️ Correction worth noting: this was a solvent break-up, not an insolvency, so there is no administrator to approach.
next: The former owner group and the new forging owner. A working plant with a dead wing and full security — not recommended.

name: Kloster Marienberg
body:
The largest surviving baroque monastery on the Mittelrhein and the largest listed monument in its district, inside the UNESCO Oberes Mittelrheintal. Run as a cold-water cure house — by the 1850s 150 rooms plus four halls. Three- to four-storey ranges around a courtyard with surviving cloister arcades. Empty since 1984.

Rare on three counts: OpenStreetMap itself asserts abandonment on the relation; three separate flight videos name it; and it cannot be demolished — the owner applied in 2007 and lost at the administrative court in 2008 and on appeal in 2009.

⚠️ Expect scaffolding and contractors — a €367,000 state grant went into securing works in 2024.
next: A named preservation society, the district heritage authority (which ordered and part-funded the securing work), and the town, which has run a redevelopment area here since 2004.

name: Michelin-Reifenwerk
body:
A truck-tyre plant producing since 1971 with about 280 jobs; production ended 31 December 2024. Multi-bay production halls, mixing and calender buildings and warehouse blocks across an 8.8-hectare footprint — the largest derelict industrial site in the region.

No press item anywhere in 2025–26 on demolition, sale or reuse. The site appears simply parked.

⚠️ Newest evidence is two years old; “still standing” is probable, not confirmed. Position approximate.
next: The corporate real-estate arm, the city development office, or the union branch that ran the closure negotiations.

name: Königsbacher-Areal
body:
Read the July 2026 press description directly: “ein großer verlassener Ort an der B9… Das Innere der Gebäude bietet sich für spannende Lost-Place-Bilder an” — giant holes in the floor where the brewing kettles stood, openings revealing hall spaces below, spiderwebs and rust. Includes a 72 m tank tower, along a 790 m frontage.

⚠️ Police are called out repeatedly for vandalism and the site is posted against entry. First demolition works were announced for 2025, so parts may already be gone.
next: The insolvency administrator of the brewery, or the investor who bought the grounds in 2018. The city said in June 2026 it will probably not buy.

name: Hotel Moselpark
body:
An early-1970s spa hotel block that housed up to 300 refugees until October 2025 — so a large room count, long corridors and a full multi-storey window grid. Building services were already failing during occupancy, with water damage taking rooms out.

⚠️ It sits inside a residential spa park with working clinics. Neighbours everywhere.
next: A named regional property group owns it; the town is the softer first call, and also holds the adjacent closed events hall.

name: Hallenbad Hermeskeil
body:
A municipal indoor pool shut on 31 March 2026 after structural damage proved far worse than expected; refurbish-versus-rebuild was still unresolved in June. A single big clear-span hall with a gallery.

The freshest empty large-span interior in the region, and the window is right now.
next: The Verbandsgemeinde owns and operated it, and the decision runs through its council — one clear counterparty.

name: Krankenhaus St. Josef
body: An empty clinic complex in the town centre, sold by its healthcare group to the town with the contract signed in May 2026 after an interim arrangement that December.
next: The cleanest route in this survey: the town is now the owner and the mayor gave on-record interviews about the purchase. ⚠️ Position approximate — the building is not in OSM.

name: Villeroy & Boch Fliesenwerk
body:
A ceramics works opened in 1879 that became “the world's largest floor-tile factory of its time”. Closure was announced in July 2022, and a rail line runs alongside the site.

⚠️ Treat as unsurveyed. There is no verified figure for site area and no description of the halls or their interior character — and it is not established that title has passed to the town.
next: The town and its mayor are named, but check the council minutes first to establish who actually owns it.

name: Ehemaliges Stadtbad
body:
Closed as a public bath in 2014, later becoming a rehearsal complex that had itself gone quiet by 2022 — “Stille, wo einst Musiker rockten”.

⚠️ Interior character and current occupancy are genuinely unverified, and the evidence is over three years old. Closest civil site to Ramstein at 24 km — check the control zone.
next: The town, or the rehearsal-space operator.

name: Ehemaliges Krankenhaus
body: A hospital whose operations ceased in 2019. ⚠️ It may already be mid-demolition — a July 2026 headline asks “Abriss in Kürze?”
next: The former healthcare operator and the town development office. Closing window — verify before driving.

name: Robert-Schuman-Haus
body:
A diocesan academy and guest house closed in August 2025 after nearly a century — a multi-wing complex with chapel, seminar halls and a guest-room tract.

The diocese describes its three large properties as “größtenteils ungenutzt und renovierungsbedürftig” and is openly seeking buyers or tenants, which makes a viewing request a legitimate door.
next: The diocesan property department; the bishop is publicly seeking investors, and the property company is named.

name: Romika-Konfektionsgebäude
body: The centrepiece of the old Romika shoe works: built 1929, listed, four floors, described as “heruntergekommen” — exactly the multi-storey window-grid type. Partly alive: people work on site.
next: The best access lead in this survey — a joiner bought it in 2023 and makes furniture there. A single named private owner. Position approximate.

name: Waldhotel Kirschweiler
body:
A former hotel complex — the December 2024 fire brigade escalated the alarm “wegen der Größe des ehemaligen Hotelkomplexes”, pulling in five brigades for a cellar fire.

⚠️ The fire was caused by a fan heater running in the cellar of a supposedly empty building. Worth knowing before you go. Evidence ~20 months old, position approximate.
next: The Verbandsgemeinde and local council; the owner is not named in press.

name: Ehemaliges Hotel Huschens
body:
A whole building complex in a hamlet of about 100 people, empty after a refugee-accommodation contract was dissolved in May 2026 following a fire-safety dispute, with a €2.3m damages suit running alongside.

⚠️ Position is a hamlet centroid, not the building.
next: The operating company, the district administration, or the mayor — who is publicly canvassing for new uses.

name: Boesner-Werk
body:
An old-established works with continuous history — “hat zwei Weltkriege überlebt”, and Covid finished it.

⚠️ Headline-level check only. Interior condition and current standing are unverified.
next: Not established. The town building office is the obvious first call.

name: Former Dorint Seehotel
body:
A large resort hotel standing empty around four years. A takeover was agreed in April 2025 and a family and wellness resort planned — but the purchase collapsed in July 2026 with public criticism of the investors.

⚠️ 19 km from Spangdahlem — check the control zone and restricted area first. An earlier sweep classed this as converted; the July 2026 evidence says otherwise. Verify.
next: The failed buyer group, or the municipality and Verbandsgemeinde.

name: Lokschuppen Konz
body:
A historic engine shed, empty for decades. A 2021 concept award to an architecture practice went nowhere once the city's cost share was clear. A single hall, modest size.

The one near-miss on flight evidence in this region: a low-view urbex walkthrough exists, though not FPV.
next: The town owns it, which makes this the easiest permission on the regional list. Position approximate.

name: Lokrichthalle, ehem. Ausbesserungswerk
body:
A wagon works until 1986. ⚠️ The hall has had no roof for years — removed for safety — and has burned internally. An open shell with a column grid: good for gates and column runs, not interior flying.

A 700-flat masterplan collapsed after 2022, but flats are going up alongside right now.
next: The developer who owns the hall and plot, or the city planning office. Active building site — position approximate.

name: Kaserne Mont Royal / ”Cyberbunker”
body:
13 hectares: two office blocks of 1,673 m² and 2,686 m², and a five-level bunker of 5,526 m² — 50 × 50 m footprint, 25 m deep — plus gatehouse, helipad and antenna field. Empty since the 2019 raid, with moisture ingress now the problem.

⚠️ Two blockers: an unresolved Bundeswehr reactivation question, and an active airfield 500 m away.
next: State-owned since 2023 with 47 registered buyers; the town and Verbandsgemeinde mayors are named. But the airspace settles it.

name: Munitionshauptdepot Rheinböllen
body:
A ghost town of ammunition bunkers and handling buildings with its own rail spur — rails vanishing into asphalt at the gate, the loading street about 100 m inside the wire. Given up in 2010.

Documented flights exist, including named drone footage and a full walkthrough. But ⚠️ July 2026 press asks directly whether it is being reactivated, inside a wider recall wave.
next: Federal property. Listed so you can rule it out deliberately rather than discover it on site.

name: Bitburg Housing
body:
Reported as 57 hectares and 75 buildings including schools, a nursery, a shopping centre, a fire station and a hospital — though those figures appeared in only one of two reports, so treat as unconfirmed. Sold in March 2026, sealed and empty to about 2028.

⚠️ About 2.8 km from an active airfield and 11 km from Spangdahlem.
next: A named project company, the airfield authority and the town — but the airspace makes it academic.

name: Straßburg-Kaserne
body:
Long vacant, conversion halted. ⚠️ The President of the Bundestag formally asked the Defence Minister to reactivate it in July 2025 and received a written open-outcome review; October 2025 press: “Konversion gestoppt”.

The surroundings are live — a major training area 10 km away, an active barracks and artillery school 1.5 km, a garrison shooting range 1 km.
next: None available. A garrison town, not a converted one. Position approximate — the pin marks the access road.

name: Eiermann-Campus (ehem. IBM)
body:
The Egon-Eiermann-designed IBM office campus — multi-storey slab blocks, vacated around 2006. Aerial footage is exterior-only, and parts have since been redeveloped into a new quarter.

⚠️ The uploader states access was refused even with a permit. Treat as an exterior subject, not an interior spot.
next: Fenced and actively refused. No realistic interior route.

name: Zeche Westerholt / Bergwerk Lippe
body:
This resolves the letter-code. A well-known freestyle video titled “Zeche W. — BIGGEST Bando in GERMANY” leaked its own location through a hidden keyword tag: this is Zeche Westerholt. A former hard-coal mine, with the flying shot in the large brick pithead and washery halls.

⚠️ The site has been progressively cleared for redevelopment. A headframe still stood recently, but expect fencing and security on an active redevelopment site.
next: A redevelopment site — no walk-in route; permission would run through the redevelopment body.

name: Camp Hitfeld
body: A former Belgian-forces garrison, now brownfield — open ground with remaining structures, used by pilots as a meet-up spot. Named in multiple video titles.
next: Open site. One of the few places pilots gather openly, so access is not the problem.

name: Flugplatz Brandis-Waldpolenz
body:
A 1930s airbase, later a Soviet garrison, closed 2005 — around 24 Eastern-Bloc barracks in pine forest, a control tower, three hangars (two badly damaged) and bunker rows. Part of the airfield is now a solar park.

Confirmed flown; a pilot comment places it “bei Leipzig”.
next: Open site — the second hangar is entered “from the left”. No security reported on the ruins.

name: Landkrankenhaus Meißen
body:
A multi-wing former county hospital — a roofless masonry ruin. The footage is a walk-through rather than a flight, so treat the FPV potential as unproven, but the structure is real and standing.

Heritage-listed.
next: Listed building — permission would run through the heritage authority.

name: HSP Hoesch Spundwand
body:
Large steel-framed rolling-mill halls with gantry-crane bays; the sheet-pile works closed in 2015.

⚠️ Earmarked for a “Smart Rhino” redevelopment and possibly demolished since — could not confirm. A viewer comment names the location, so single-source. Position approximate.
next: The entrance is “a bit hidden” per the footage; a redevelopment site, so expect fencing.

name: Schaufelradbagger ”Bagger 1473”
body:
A 1964 bucket-wheel excavator left on a former opencast mine — a protected monument, locally the “Blaues Wunder”. A structure spot rather than a building: a vast steel lattice to thread.

⚠️ Security intervened during one shoot, and people free-climb it.
next: A listed monument with active security. Not a casual walk-up.

name: Möbelwelt Zick
body:
A three-level furniture flagship of 18,000 m², completed 1997 and closed 2004 — heavily stripped and vandalised. Big open retail floorplates with escalator voids: a very different flying problem from a factory hall.

Two pilots flew it; independent urbex names it. ⚠️ Position is town-level only — the building is not in OSM.
next: The owner, via the town. Position approximate — confirm before driving.

name: ”Area One” — ehem. Sonderwaffenlager
body:
A Cold-War US special-weapons (nuclear) storage depot on a wooded plateau — bunkers, guard towers and fence lines, now preserved by a heritage interest group as a memorial and accessible to hikers.

Confirmed flown: a named FPV video explores it. ~111 km from you, and the maintained-memorial status makes this one of the rare restricted-type sites you can actually approach.

⚠️ Position is the municipality — the depot sits about 2 km north-east; confirm the exact point before travelling.
next: Contact the interest group that preserves the site (IG Area One). A memorial with an active custodian is a real permission route, not a locked gate.

name: Gerresheimer Glashütte
body:
The former Gerresheimer glassworks — the historic Tonnenhalle and water tower survive amid a new “Glasmacherviertel” quarter. Confirmed flown in a named FPV video.

⚠️ The site is under active redevelopment, so expect security and construction; the standing halls are the target, not the built-over parcels.
next: The redevelopment body, via the city. Only the heritage structures are safe bets now.

name: Tonwerk ”1818” / Boltze
body:
A clay and kaolin processing works described as one of the region's oldest industrial operations — historically linked to an 1830s brickworks once called the largest in Prussia. A named FPV video explored it in 2025, so it is standing and enterable.

⚠️ Position is village-level; the exact building is unconfirmed.
next: None named. The village is small — a look from the road would pin it.

name: Tuchfabrik Wülfing — Werk Dahlerau
body:
The monumental former cloth factory (Tuchfabrik) of Johann Wülfing & Sohn, Werk Dahlerau — a four-storey red-brick spinning mill with round-arch windows and a stepped gable, extensive sawtooth weaving-shed roofs, a tall round brick boiler-house chimney and a distinctive circular concrete structure, wedged on a tight loop of the dammed River Wupper. Known in the FPV scene as the “Triangle bando” for the wedge-shaped parcel where the Wupper and the Obergraben mill-race converge to a point.

Identified from the pilot's own footage and his own FPV-sim reconstruction of the same buildings, cross-checked with OpenStreetMap — the boiler-house chimney (OSM node) is explicitly described there as the chimney of the former Tuchfabrik Johann Wülfing & Sohn — and confirmed on satellite (round chimney, circular structure, sawtooth roofs, the Wupper weir, and Wülfingstraße/Tuchmacherweg).

⚠️ The derelict core (brick spinning mill, chimney, circular structure) is a well-documented Bergisches-Land Lost Place — broken windows, graffiti, trees growing inside — but the wider complex is partly in active use (a metalworks, a joinery, a furniture store and offices occupy some halls, with a small Wülfing-Museum and converted lofts nearby). This is private property with people around, not a free-roam ruin.
next: No open access — private and partly occupied. The derelict wings carry roof/floor-collapse and unstable-masonry risk, and the dammed Wupper, its weir and the mill-race canals run right alongside (drowning risk). Approach only with the owner's permission; the Wülfing-Museum next door is the natural first contact.

name: Flugplatz Sperenberg — Control Tower
body:
⚠️ EXTREME UXO — the ground fuses the historic Kummersdorf gunnery proving range with the USSR’s largest airbase in the GDR, so unexploded ordnance is pervasive off hard tracks. The OSM-confirmed control tower now stands inside dense regrowth pine; a large hangar slab & wall, aprons and fuel-depot ruins lie about 1 km west.

Hazards: ⚠️ asbestos, collapsing floors, open shafts and total isolation with no reception.
next: Former Soviet military land (now forestry and nature area); entry is Hausfriedensbruch and genuinely UXO-lethal, so treat the ground as no-go and verify NOTAM plus any restricted-area status before any flight.

name: Flugplatz Zerbst — Control Tower Ruin
body:
⚠️ Asbestos & collapse — the roofless control-tower ruin (OSM: ehem. Tower) sits at the wooded western edge of the former Soviet airbase, with the derelict Baracke barracks about 350 m north and a shelter row nearby.

Keep clear: a large solar park now covers the runway just to the east, and a club gliding strip is still active at the far eastern end.
next: Former military ground beside an operating solar park and an active gliding strip; ground entry is Hausfriedensbruch and the airfield carries live glider traffic, so verify NOTAM/ATZ and stay off the panels before any flight.

name: Flugplatz Alt Daber — Arched Shelter
status: Woodland HAS east of solar park
body:
⚠️ Possible residual UXO in this Wittstock-area former Soviet airbase; the pin is an earth-covered arched shelter (Bogendeckung AU-16/3), one of a dispersal cluster of about eight ringing a loop taxiway in woodland.

Keep clear: a solar park covers the central and western field roughly 700 m west (stay off the panels); the medieval Daberturm keep in the village is a maintained monument, not part of this site.
next: Former military woodland, largely private; entering the earth-covered shelters risks collapse and confined-space hazards and is Hausfriedensbruch, and any flight should verify NOTAM/ATZ and avoid the solar park.

name: Jüterbog Altes Lager — Garrison Barracks
body:
⚠️ Regional UXO — Altes Lager lies inside the former Jüterbog Truppenübungsplatz (military training area), so stay on firm ground. The pin is a long derelict barracks in the reclaiming forest of this historic garrison, one of Germany’s oldest, with many more roofless blocks around it.

Keep clear: the airfield itself is active (Sonderlandeplatz plus model flying) about 1.6 km south — pin only the derelict Kaserne. The Altes Lager water tower further south is a preserved landmark, not a ruin.
next: Former military garrison land, partly private; entry is Hausfriedensbruch with asbestos/collapse and regional UXO risk and the nearby aerodrome is live, so verify NOTAM/ATZ and keep clear of the operational field before any flight.

name: Gutsanlage Gentzrode
body:
Protected 19th-century estate north of Neuruppin whose manor house and Moorish-style brick granary stand as decaying, part-roofless ruins in open woodland.

Turkish investors bought the site in 2010 with restoration plans, but no works followed for years. ⚠️ Heritage monument in severe decay with only emergency stabilisation since 2022; unstable masonry, roof holes and open floors.
next: Open estate grounds, but the buildings are a listed Baudenkmal in private ownership; seek the owner's permission before any close approach or entry.

name: Kraftwerk Heegermühle (Kraftwerk Finow)
body:
Historic AEG power plant of 1909 on the Finow canal, shut down in 1991 and left as a derelict industrial ruin. The original hall still stands; a proposed reactivation into a semi-public cultural and leisure space has not been carried out.

⚠️ Hazardous industrial ruin with an active electrical substation (Umspannwerk) immediately to the west, so keep well clear of live high-voltage equipment.
next: The plant sits on private industrial land beside the Finow canal and a live substation; ask locally before approaching and stay clear of the energised switchyard.

name: JVA Frankfurt (Oder)
body:
Former Stasi-era prison (JVA) that closed on 1 December 2013 and has stood empty since, marketed for sale with no new use found and not demolished. The walled cell blocks, sports yard and perimeter wall remain intact.

⚠️ Sealed secure structure; an active administrative/justice complex with staff parking adjoins it to the east, so the setting is sensitive.
next: The compound is walled and sealed with no public access, and an active institutional complex sits immediately east, so keep any flight discreet and outside its airspace.

name: Bahnhof Brandenburg-Altstadt
body:
The historic reception building (Empfangsgebäude, 1904) of the Altstädtischer Bahnhof is abandoned; a roof-truss fire on 4 February 2025 severely damaged it and caused a partial collapse. Passengers now use only a modern platform shelter.

⚠️ Live railway — the line is still served hourly by RB51 trains, and the fire-damaged structure is unstable.
next: The derelict building stands directly beside operating tracks and platforms; there is no safe or legal ground access, and drones must stay clear of live rail and rail traffic.

name: Ehem. JVA Spremberg
body:
Former juvenile detention facility (Jugendhaftanstalt) closed in spring 2004 and abandoned ever since; a well-known regional lost place, with inmate writings and artwork reportedly still surviving in the cells. The grey cell blocks stand amid overgrown grounds behind a perimeter fence.

⚠️ Sealed secure structure with barred cells and decayed interiors; parts of the wider site to the north-west appear reused.
next: The prison buildings are fenced and closed, so entry is trespassing on secured property; treat this as an exterior-only overflight.

name: Wulfen station (Bahnhof Wulfen)
body:
A two-storey brick station building of 1879, protected as a monument, empty and disused for years; the goods shed alongside has already been reduced to its foundations.

⚠️ Beside a LIVE line — Wulfen is still served hourly by the RE 14, so trains pass at speed. Stay off the tracks and clear of the platform edge.
next: Plainly visible from Kleiner Ring and the station forecourt; the building sits on railway-boundary land, so view and film only from the public side.

name: Nachrodt old station ruin
body:
Roofless, overgrown remains of the former Nachrodt station, abandoned for decades on the narrow strip between the railway and the river Lenne.

⚠️ Beside a LIVE electrified main line (Ruhr-Sieg route, 15 kV overhead) with fast trains, and the masonry is unstable — keep well clear of the tracks, the wires and the collapsing walls.
next: Reached on foot from Stenglingser Weg and the riverside path; it lies on open lineside land, so treat the railway as off-limits and keep your distance from the tracks.

name: Olympiastadion ghost station
body:
Built for the 1972 Olympics and closed in 1988, this S-Bahn station has been left to decay ever since; the platform roof and structures survive under graffiti and scrub as part of the listed Olympiapark ensemble.

⚠️ Urban airspace — dense city setting beside a busy ring road. The spur is dead (no live trains), but expect drops, debris and rusted steel on the decaying platforms.
next: In central Munich in the Olympiapark green corridor on city-owned land pending redevelopment; check drone and airspace rules carefully before any flight over this built-up area.

name: Gladenbach old station (Alter Bahnhof)
body:
The old Gladenbach station stands empty on the edge of town beside its lifted, grassed-over track bed, the platform side now open ground.

⚠️ The line here is disused (no live trains), but this is an unsecured, decaying building — watch for rotten floors, broken glass and open pits.
next: On former railway land next to a sports ground and small industrial units; approach from the public path but treat the building itself as private, disused property.

name: TU Clausthal swimming hall
body:
The swimming hall of TU Clausthal, a listed monument, has been out of use since 2007 because it is structurally unsafe, and survives as an empty, decaying shell while the university seeks funds to save it.

⚠️ Officially unsafe (baufällig) with a drained pool basin — real collapse and fall hazards, and any standing water can carry Legionella. Do not enter.
next: Set in the Bergakademie university quarter; it is a protected but derelict building on university land, so view from the surrounding streets and seek permission before approaching.

name: Amecke lido (Freibad Amecke)
body:
The former Amecke lido on the south shore of the Sorpesee lies abandoned and fenced off — drained basins, cracked decks and a derelict changing block slowly reverting to nature.

⚠️ Empty concrete basins mean deep drops and loose edges, and any standing water can carry Legionella; parts of the overgrown site also show ground disturbance, so tread carefully.
next: Beside the lakeshore road and car park near the Heimathafen restaurant; the pool is fenced private land, so view from the public path unless the owner grants access.

name: St Barbara church, Hückelhoven
body:
A brick church of 1933, deconsecrated at its final Mass in September 2016 and standing empty since; still treated as a protected monument with no confirmed new use.

⚠️ A long-sealed church interior means pigeon and bat guano and a histoplasmosis risk, and any bats present are legally protected — do not disturb roosts.
next: In a residential quarter and outwardly intact; it is diocesan property (Bistum Aachen), so admire and film from the street and ask the parish before seeking entry.

name: St Barbara church, Duisburg-Rheinhausen
body:
A modernist church of 1960 to 1961 with a striking pyramid roof and a separate round tower, given up as a church in 2011 and empty ever since; listed as a monument apart from the tower.

⚠️ A sealed, long-empty church — droppings inside carry a histoplasmosis risk and any bat roosts are legally protected. Keep out of the interior.
next: Stands openly on a residential corner next to the WOMA factory; the roof films well from the public road, but the building is private, so seek permission for any closer access.

name: St Vitus hospital church, Gerolzhofen
body:
A Baroque hospital church of 1710, a protected monument, profaned in July 2025 after more than 600 years and now empty in the old town while its owner, the town hospital foundation, decides its future.

⚠️ A recently sealed church interior — guano and histoplasmosis risk and possible protected bat roosts; the surrounding old town is tightly built, so mind people and property below.
next: Right in the historic centre on Spitalstraße; it belongs to the Spitalstiftung Gerolzhofen, so seek their permission and film considerately over a busy townscape.

name: FDGB holiday home “Hermann Duncker”
body:
FDGB ”Hermann Duncker” — built 1909 as ”Villa Waldpark”, a trade-union holiday home abandoned since 1990. A roughly 55×81 m ruin on the Barenberg above Schierke.

⚠️ Severe internal collapse with missing floors & walls, and likely asbestos in later fittings; occupied holiday lets adjoin the plot.
next: Private ruin on the Barenberg; enter only with the owner’s permission and never via the adjoining holiday lets.

name: Ferienlager Repente (youth camp)
body:
