GDR children’s Ferienlager by the Zootzensee near Repente; a documented lost place with weathered façades & overgrown paths. A light-roofed central hall still stands among rows of decaying cabins.

⚠️ Isolation in remote lakeside woods, open water, roof/floor collapse and probable asbestos-cement roofing.
next: Remote private site with no public access — seek the landowner’s consent before visiting.

name: Harz sanatorium for the blind
body:
Former sanatorium for the blind & partially sighted near Wildemann, now disused and standing alone in dense Harz woodland reached by a single forest track.

⚠️ Strong isolation (little phone signal), advancing decay/collapse and likely asbestos; do not go alone.
next: On private forest land reached by a single track; ask permission and do not visit solo.

name: Former Vital Hotel Sitzendorf
body:
The former Vital Hotel, once one of the valley’s largest GDR hotels; empty since the mid-1990s and badly fire-damaged in 2010. The large shell still stands beside the town open-air pool.

⚠️ Fire-weakened structure with high collapse risk and asbestos; a demolition order exists, so it may soon disappear.
next: Fenced private demolition site; view from the public road unless the owner grants access.

name: Former Katzhütte youth hostel
body:
The former Katzhütte Jugendherberge, recorded as permanently closed; an intact but disused building on the village street in the Schwarza valley.

⚠️ Standing empty among occupied houses, with possible asbestos in fittings. Respect neighbours’ privacy.
next: Private closed hostel in an occupied village — no public entry; ask the owner first.

name: Bad Suderode Kur centre
body:
The Kurzentrum in the still-active spa town of Bad Suderode — closed since 2013 and standing empty in the town centre; the working Kurhotel & spa buildings are separate.

⚠️ Sealed heritage-era block with likely asbestos; a very visible town-centre location.
next: Council/spa-owned vacant building in a public area; permission is required to enter.

name: Sonnenhotel Residenz Hohenzollern
body:
Sonnenhotel Residenz Hohenzollern, a closed Braunlage hotel; the operating company has been dissolved and OSM & local press record it as no longer opening. The 3-storey building stands intact.

⚠️ Private and likely secured; possible asbestos. A resale/reopening is possible, so re-check first.
next: Private hotel property, presumed secured; obtain permission and re-verify its status before travelling.

name: Former Seesen municipal hospital
body:
Former municipal hospital (latterly Asklepios), Seesen — vacant, with the owner seeking a buyer and reported vandalism. A large intact but decaying complex on Lautenthaler Straße.

⚠️ Likely asbestos, internal hazards & possible security; occupied buildings stand nearby.
next: Private hospital site owned by Asklepios; entry needs the owner’s permission.

name: Former “Bacchus Ruh” care home
body:
The former ”Bacchus Ruh” senior care home, a disused 3-storey building in Lerbach near Osterode; the neighbouring block is an ex-hotel now converted to flats.

⚠️ Empty building with possible asbestos, and an old mine adit close by. Respect the adjoining residents.
next: Private former care home among occupied homes; seek permission before approaching.

name: Former DRK children’s home
body:
Former DRK (Red Cross) children’s home in Burg auf Fehmarn, mapped as abandoned; a standing building in a residential street, distinct from the active care centre beside it.

⚠️ Status rests on OpenStreetMap tagging — verify before relying on it; occupied homes & a care facility adjoin it.
next: Privately owned in a residential street; verify its status and ask permission before any visit.

name: Former “Haus Frohsinn” children’s home
body:
Former private children’s home ”Haus Frohsinn” at Burgstaaken harbour, Fehmarn; a 2-storey building mapped as abandoned amid working harbour businesses.

⚠️ Status is from OpenStreetMap only — verify; a busy harbour & open water lie alongside.
next: Private plot within a working harbour; confirm ownership and current status before approaching.

name: Nußknackerbaude (ex-hotel)
body:
The Nußknackerbaude, a permanently closed hotel-restaurant in the toy-making village of Seiffen; the building stands empty among active guest houses.

⚠️ Closed building, plus ⚠️ open historic mine shafts & pinges nearby (signed ”Lebensgefahr”). Possible asbestos.
next: Privately owned closed hotel; ask permission and keep well clear of the unsecured mine workings.

name: Howinol refinery ruin
body:
Confirmed standing ruin of the Holtz & Willemsen (Howinol) technical-oil and fat refinery on the Rhine bank at Hohenbudberg, long abandoned, heavily overgrown, with a wrecked barge still at the old jetty.

⚠️ Oil and chemical contamination is likely across the whole plot, which sits on private industrial land right beside the active Krefeld-Uerdingen Chempark.
next: Fenced private riverside industrial land with no public access; best seen from the Rhine dyke path or from the opposite bank.

name: Mersmann cement works
body:
Genuinely derelict cement works south of Beckum, ringed by woodland, with roofless kiln halls, a landmark white clinker-storage dome and stagnant quarry ponds. Beckum still runs active cement plants (Phoenix and Kollenbach); this Mersmann works is the abandoned one.

⚠️ Collapsing concrete, open silos and pits, and probable asbestos; treat all interiors as unsafe.
next: Unsecured ruin on private land deep in forest; reached on foot along woodland tracks south of Beckum.

name: Schönwalde Soviet airbase
body:
Sprawling derelict garrison of the former Soviet airfield at Schönwalde, with rows of roofless barracks, service buildings and hangars being swallowed by forest beside the abandoned grass runway.

⚠️ Unexploded ordnance is a genuine risk on this former Soviet military ground; structures are collapsing, the land is private and part-fenced, and Berlin controlled airspace begins not far to the south-east.
next: Private, partly fenced ex-military land with no sanctioned access; entered informally and entirely at own risk.

name: SEZ Berlin
body:
The huge GDR-era Sport- und Erholungszentrum (Sport & Recreation Centre) on Landsberger Allee stands empty and decaying, one of the best-known lost places in central Berlin, its finger-roofed pool halls still recognisable.

⚠️ Dense-city site inside Berlin restricted (ED-R) drone airspace; a 2026 demolition for housing and a school was halted in February 2026 over species protection but still looms.
next: Sealed, monitored building on a busy city junction; no legal access and low flying here is airspace-restricted.

name: Alte Ziegelei Eilsdorf
body:
A brickworks founded around 1888 and closed in 1965, now an overgrown ruin hidden in a cluster of trees at a field junction, with a surviving brick chimney and old clay-pit landforms close by.

⚠️ The roofs and floors have collapsed and the brickwork is unstable, making this a genuinely dangerous ruin. It is not heritage-listed and has not been demolished or redeveloped.
next: It sits on private farmland and scrub off the Eilsdorf–Diekhof lane with no formal access, and the collapsing masonry makes entering hazardous.

name: Brodauer Mühle
body:
A gallery Dutch windmill built in 1864 that burned down in November 2005; only the octagonal brick base and some charred timbers survive, standing beside the road on the edge of a golf course.

It is a protected Kulturdenkmal. A reconstruction was attempted but failed, and the ruin has since been offered for sale with an obligation to rebuild it.
next: The brick base stands on the grounds of the Brodauer Mühle golf course beside the L-road, so ask the golf club first as it is monument-protected private land.

name: Ehem. Waldkrankenhaus Drangstedt
body:
A wartime reserve hospital, later a nursing home and military camp in the Knüppelholz forest; most barracks were demolished in the 1990s, but about four overgrown wooden barracks still stand among the old foundation slabs.

⚠️ The surviving barracks are collapse-prone (einsturzgefährdet). They also shelter one of northern Germany’s largest bat colonies, and part of the grounds is a fenced-off timber-treatment yard.
next: The forest is publicly accessible off the L120, but the barracks are unstable and protected as a bat roost, and the timber-treatment yard must not be entered.

name: Flakbatterie Langwarden
body:
Remains of the WWII naval anti-aircraft battery Langwarden, operational from 1940: several concrete gun emplacements and a part-buried command bunker on the grazing marsh behind the dyke, near the beach by Fedderwardersiel.

This coast lies inside the Nationalpark Niedersächsisches Wattenmeer, where drone flights are prohibited (§21h LuftVO) without a case-by-case exemption. ⚠️ Residual UXO cannot be excluded at a wartime flak site, and ⚠️ the adjoining tidal flats bring fast-rising water & soft mud.
next: The emplacements sit on open coastal marsh reachable on foot from the Langwarder Groden car park, but any drone flight needs a national-park exemption and the mudflats must not be entered near a rising tide.

name: Sondermunitionslager Lahn
body:
Derelict former NATO special-ammunition (nuclear) depot, abandoned 1992; about a dozen earth-covered storage bunkers plus the guard & maintenance buildings still stand, heavily overgrown and vandalised — not reactivated.

⚠️ ED-R 34 restricted airspace (WTD 91 Meppen weapons range) lies ~2 km W/SW; the site is just outside it, but check NOTAM/activation before flying. ⚠️ Parts of the wider grounds are now the fenced Solarpark Lahn.
next: Former Bundeswehr land, perimeter fences largely gone but treat as private; the wooded bunker row is open ground, the adjacent solar park is fenced.

name: Pilsumer Ziegelei
body:
Standing Hoffmann ring-kiln brickworks ruin (1898–~1972). The massive kiln hall stands roofless beside a round kiln and a chimney stump; an OSM-mapped office-building ruin sits ~110 m NW.

⚠️ Severe collapse danger and flooded kiln chambers; privately owned, a well-known but forbidden lost place.
next: Private land, entry only with the owner’s permission; the ruins are posted and structurally unsafe.

name: Johanni-Mühle
body:
Fire-gutted brick windmill torso — a gallery-Dutch mill (1865) that burned out on 21 Aug 2000, now a secured bare tower stump with no cap and no sails, at the field edge in the village.

Maintained by a local mill association that hopes to rebuild but has done only minor work.
next: Association-owned and roadside-visible; easy to view and photograph from public ground — respect the site and neighbours.

name: Kinderheim Birkenhöhe
body:
Abandoned children’s convalescent home, empty ~20 years. Two brick buildings stand in overgrown woodland; the main one keeps its red-tiled roof but the interior is wrecked with collapsed ceilings.

⚠️ Reported cordoned off since 2024/25 and decaying fast — securing or demolition may be near.
next: Private property, now fenced/cordoned off; entering is trespassing and the interior is unsafe.

name: Schule Neuhof
body:
Derelict heritage-listed brick school on Neuhöfer Damm, one of the last two buildings of the demolished Neuhof village. Empty 15+ years, still standing into 2026 with a failing, water-damaged roof and no redevelopment.

⚠️ Hamburg Port Authority land inside the working port, with CCTV nearby.
next: Fenced HPA port property with cameras nearby; not openly accessible and Hamburg’s urban/port drone rules require a permit.

name: Lagerhalle Stresemannstraße
body:
Abandoned warehouse (Lagerhalle) in a dense block off Stresemannstraße; OSM still tags it abandoned as of April 2026, with no demolition or redevelopment reported.

A backyard/courtyard structure, hard to read as derelict from directly overhead.
next: Private, abandoned building in a residential block; assume fenced and structurally unsafe — no open access.

name: Bergbaurelikt Brechwerk (Lemberg)
body:
Roughly 12 m grey ore-crushing works (Brechwerk) standing derelict in forest on the Lemberg, a relic of the Lemberg mercury (cinnabar) field worked into the early 20th century. OpenStreetMap maps the ruin at this exact point as a disused building=industrial with a former headframe (headframe=yes, height 12.3 m).

⚠️ A 12 m unsecured industrial ruin — fall & collapse risk — ringed by old spoil embankments with flooded former workings in the woods nearby. This is the isolated relic, distinct from the Schmittenstollen show-mine about 1.4 km NE — do not confuse the two.
next: It stands on unfenced forest land reachable on the Lemberg walking trails; nothing is posted, so approach the fragile ruin entirely at your own risk.

name: Bewetterungsschornstein Grube Rennseiter
body:
Isolated brick ventilation chimney (Bewetterungsschornstein) of the former Grube Rennseiter slate mine, on the old roofing-slate plateau about 1.7 km ENE of Kaub above the Rhine, where pasture meets woodland and a scrub thicket has grown up around its base. OpenStreetMap records it as a disused man_made=chimney, surveyed still standing in March 2024.

⚠️ The surrounding woods are riddled with the old mine's workings — the Oberer Rennseiter-Stolln and Rennseiter Stolln 2 adits lie ~150–250 m off and the Grube Ernestine shaft ~500 m away, several tagged as open holes / sinkholes. Real open-adit & subsidence hazard once you leave the path.
next: The chimney is on unfenced land reachable on foot via the Kaub mining-relic trails; it is unsecured, and the nearby open adits and shafts make straying off the path dangerous.

name: Kirsch GmbH (former works)
body:
Former Kirsch GmbH works on Biewerer Straße in the Mosel valley on Trier's northern edge, which built generators & emergency-power systems until the PRETTL group closed the plant in 2017; it has stood empty since. Weathered sawtooth-roofed production halls with a fenced yard still fill the plot.

⚠️ A fire tore through a vacant hall here in May 2025 — fire-damaged, unstable structures plus likely asbestos in the old industrial roofing. The site is fenced private land.
next: The works is fenced, private and vacant; it is plainly visible from Biewerer Straße, but entry is Hausfriedensbruch and the fire-damaged halls are dangerous, so do not go in without the owner's permission.

name: UNILUX Piesport — disused works
body:
Former UNILUX window-and-door factory (the Piesport plant) on the Mosel valley floor at Niederemmel; the Piesport company was dissolved and deleted from the register, with production consolidated at the firm's Salmtal headquarters. OpenStreetMap maps the site as a disused works (disused:man_made=works), the large production hall still standing while the adjoining yard has been cleared to bare ground.

The hall looks structurally intact rather than dramatically ruinous, so whether the interior is genuinely abandoned or merely mothballed is uncertain. ⚠️ Private commercial land; a separate active business and the Moseltalhalle stand close by to the west.
next: It is a disused works on fenced private commercial land beside a roundabout; view it from the public road and seek the owner's permission before approaching or flying close.

name: Former Kreiskrankenhaus Schramberg
body:
Reinforced-concrete district hospital opened 1965 on the Bühle hillside above town; closed in 2011, and after the follow-on MVZ practice left in 2019 the block has stood completely empty.

It is city-owned inside the Bühlepark redevelopment area; a housing conversion (PLAN 7 & Activ Immobilien) is planned but stuck in negotiation as of 2025/26. ⚠️ Large sealed building with the usual derelict-hospital interior hazards.
next: City-owned, fenced and secured — there is no public access, and the derelict-hospital interior is unsafe.

name: ZF-Arena (former Messehalle)
body:
Landmark 1960s exhibition hall with a heritage-listed suspended cable roof, reopened in 2004 as the ZF-Arena (home of VfB Friedrichshafen volleyball).

⚠️ It was shut suddenly in September 2020 after its roof suspension cables corroded — an acute collapse risk. Demolition was decided (Feb 2024) and permitted (Dec 2024) but not yet carried out; a school sports hall is to replace it. ⚠️ The hall sits ~2.6 km from Bodensee Airport, inside its control zone.
next: Fenced off for collapse risk and inside the Bodensee Airport control zone, so there is no lawful public access and any drone flight needs ATC clearance.

name: Former Bahnschwellenwerk Kirchseeon
body:
Railway-sleeper creosote-impregnation works, derelict since 1982; almost everything was razed in 1964, leaving the 1895 operations building and the listed 27 m water tower (empty since 1993) standing amid an overgrown slab field south of the station.

⚠️ The ground is heavily contaminated — coal-tar creosote (PAH) plus mercury from the earliest impregnation; partial remediation ran 2005–2016. A large ECE housing scheme is in planning but nothing is built yet.
next: A fenced, contaminated Industriebrache — entry is hazardous (tar/creosote residues) and unlawful, so the tower is best seen from the public edges.

name: Berghotel Kalteck
body:
Post-war ski-boom mountain hotel on the ~750 m Kalteck saddle in the Bavarian Forest; its ski lift is out of service and the hotel has been abandoned for about 15 years.

Ownership passed from Seitz → Penzkofer and redevelopment ideas remain purely theoretical as of Feb 2026 (water supply unresolved). ⚠️ Long-abandoned and structurally decayed. Note the separate Kalteck-Gasthaus & hikers' car park ~250 m east are still active — not part of the ruin.
next: Privately owned and structurally unsafe; the saddle has a public hikers' car park but the hotel itself is off-limits without the owner's permission.

name: Former Polytec plant (Polytec-Areal)
body:
Former automotive plastic-interior plant on Titschendorfer Straße in the Buckenreuth part of town; production ceased around 2010 and the big halls have been a standing industrial brownfield since 2012.

It was sold in 2022 to a machinery firm that made no visible changes, to local disappointment, and no demolition or reuse has been reported. ⚠️ Sealed derelict works with possible legacy contamination from plastics production (unconfirmed).
next: Privately owned and fenced — no public access; view it from Titschendorfer Straße rather than entering.

name: Alte Ziegelei Mühlingen “Berenberg”
body:
Former brickworks (Ziegelei) on a wooded lane at Berenberg, mapped in OpenStreetMap as building:condition=mainly_ruinous and disused, its old kiln chimney still standing. Imagery shows a long weathered-roof hall & outbuildings in an overgrown clearing.

⚠️ Ruinous masonry & likely partial roof collapse. The reactivated Ablachtalbahn heritage railway and its Mühlingen-Zoznegg halt pass about 90 m east.
next: Standing derelict at Berenberg 1 on private land beside a minor road; visible from the lane but enter only with the owner's permission.

name: Heeresmunitionsanstalt Straß “Muna”
status: WWII munitions depot, bunkers in forest
body:
WWII army munitions depot (Muna) whose roughly 90 earth-covered magazine bunkers survive as ruins scattered through the Straßer Wald. Now decommissioned federal (BImA) forest earmarked for civilian use — not an active military site.

⚠️ Bunkers are earth-mounded & hidden under dense canopy, so individual structures cannot be pinned from satellite; expect UXO risk, unstable concrete & open shafts.
next: Open woodland laced with public tracks and no visible perimeter fence, but it is federal land with genuine UXO and collapse hazards — treat as enter-at-your-own-risk and check local rules first.

name: Bahnhof Langenneufnach
body:
Small trackside station on the Staudenbahn (Gessertshausen–Türkheim), a branch line whose scheduled traffic ended and that now carries only occasional heritage trains (operator SWU Verkehr). A modest station building & a former goods yard with a disused siding sit by the single track.

The building still stands and looks structurally intact rather than dramatically ruinous, so its vacant-vs-used status is uncertain.
next: Trackside in the village beside a line still used for occasional heritage runs; view from the public level crossing and lane and do not walk on the rails.

name: Schloss Reinhardsbrunn
body:
Neo-Gothic ducal Schloss set in an English landscape park; a GDR-era hotel until 1990, then left to rot by absentee investors. Thuringia expropriated it (final Feb 2021) for the Stiftung Thüringer Schlösser und Gärten, but it stays empty and slowly decaying — only emergency roof repairs have been done.

⚠️ Managed state heritage site with caretakers; the red-roofed estate & restaurant buildings just NE are active (cars, parking). The fabric is fragile and partly unsafe.
next: The park is public so the exterior is easy to see, but the Schloss itself is fenced state property with caretakers — seek permission from the Stiftung before approaching or flying close.

name: Former hospital complex (radial pavilions)
body:
Large disused hospital / sanatorium built as pavilions radiating from a central roundel, deep in the Dübener Heide forest off Reinharzer Straße (near Spatenweg). Long abandoned: roofs are caving in, trees have fallen across the wards and the woods are swallowing the access roads.

⚠️ Structurally dangerous (collapsed roofs & floors); one corner shows partial demolition/clearance, so an owner may occasionally be on site.
next: Unsecured but private, fenced forest land in the Dübener Heide nature park with homes close by to the west and south — no permission is posted, so approach and overflight are entirely at your own risk.

name: Kraftwerk Plessa
body:
One of the oldest surviving lignite power plants (1926/27) — machine hall, boiler house, gatehouse & two chimneys kept largely in original condition as an Industriedenkmal. Per Wikipedia it is currently (2024) closed to normal visits, enterable only via ”lost-place” arrangement.

⚠️ Borderline: a maintained monument (roof PV, museum gGmbH), not free-decaying. Asbestos plausible; mind fenced/idle-plant areas.
next: Heritage monument presently closed to visitors — arrange access with the owning museum gGmbH.

name: Grube Göttelborn
status: Winding towers + coal wash, part reused
body:
The white winding tower (”Weißer Riese”, Schacht IV) & the Schacht III headframe, plus the vast Kohlenwäsche (≈49.34269, 7.03583), stand as listed but largely unconverted ruins — alongside an active business & solar park (”Zukunftsstandort Göttelborn”).

⚠️ Asbestos plausible; large empty hall = fall/collapse risk. Shaft sealed with a ~70 m concrete plug.
next: The outdoor heritage boulevard and Himmelspfeil walkway are public; building interiors are fenced — ask the site managers.

name: Filmfabrik Wolfen (Agfa/ORWO)
status: Derelict film halls; active chem park
body:
About ¾ of the old Agfa/ORWO film works is demolished; surviving halls stand derelict on cleared meadows beside the fully active Chemiepark Bitterfeld-Wolfen. The preserved Gießerei building (0112) ~150 m north houses the film museum (that is the ”official” 51.6566,12.2626 point).

⚠️ Major chemical Altlasten/groundwater-contamination zone; asbestos & collapse in the halls. Some halls are reused by small film firms; the surrounding chemical park is fenced & secured.
next: The film museum is public, but the derelict halls lie within a secured active chemical park with no free access.

name: Bärenquell-Brauerei
body:
Large brick brewery (1882–1994) — Sud-/Maschinenhaus, Bierlager with cooling tower & admin buildings stand derelict after ~30 years empty, with trees in the windows and heavy graffiti. Conversion permits exist but building has barely started (as of 2024).

⚠️ Heritage-listed; asbestos, ~30-yr decay & arson damage = collapse/fire risk. Berlin controlled airspace — check drone rules.
next: Private and fenced; parts open during interim-use events (markets, cinema), otherwise ask the owner.

name: Ringlok- und Rundlokschuppen Pankow-Heinersdorf
body:
Two heritage-protected engine sheds on the old Heinersdorf yard — the 1901–06 semicircular Ringlokschuppen (this point) and the 1893 circular Rundlokschuppen ~170 m SW (≈52.5779, 13.4303, OSM). Long derelict; re-roofed/scaffolded for stabilisation since ~2021.

⚠️ A Berlin court barred demolition (Dec 2024); still part of the stalled ”Pankower Tor” scheme. Asbestos plausible; active stabilisation/construction hazards. Berlin controlled airspace.
next: Private, fenced former-railway land with no public access — permission required.

name: Herrenhaus Pinnow
status: Derelict manor in park by the pond
body:
Large derelict Herrenhaus on the edge of a wooded park and pond; the surrounding Gutshof (farm buildings with fresh red roofs) is partly in use, but the manor itself stands empty under an old, dark, deteriorating roof.

Heritage-listed & private property. ⚠️ Watch for masonry & roof collapse near the walls.
next: Private, heritage-listed estate; view from the farm track or park edge only, no entry.

name: Gutshaus Tützpatz
body:
Long two-storey Gutshaus standing empty in an overgrown park; the roof is patchy and rust-stained with a partly open, tarped section.

Heritage-listed & private property. ⚠️ Roof & masonry collapse risk; do not enter.
next: Private, heritage-listed manor; view from the estate lane or satellite only, no entry.

name: Gut Neparmitz
body:
Two-storey Gutshaus with a hipped roof standing amid a completely overgrown, jungle-like park on Rügen; clearly long abandoned.

Heritage-listed & private property. ⚠️ Possible masonry & roof decay near the walls.
next: Private, heritage-listed manor on Rügen; view from the road or satellite only, no entry.

name: Gutshaus Mollenstorf
body:
Long Gutshaus range on the edge of the village park; the manor end has a mottled, deteriorating roof and the grounds are overgrown, a standing but derelict building.

Heritage-listed & private property. ⚠️ Masonry & roof collapse risk.
next: Private, heritage-listed manor; view from the village lane or satellite only, no entry.

name: Gutshaus Barkvieren
status: Ruined manor hidden under tree cover
body:
Gutshaus recorded as a ruin, standing within a dense stand of mature trees beside an active farmyard; the building is hidden under the canopy on satellite and appears ruinous.

Heritage-listed & private property. ⚠️ Likely roofless — masonry & collapse hazard.
next: Private property beside a working farm; view from the field track only, no entry.

name: Gutshaus Altwigshagen
status: Roofless manor ruin in the woods
body:
Roofless shell of the Gutshaus, its interior walls open to the sky with the wooded park closing in around it.

⚠️ Hazardous roofless ruin — serious masonry & collapse risk. Private property, do not enter.
next: Private, overgrown ruin near the lake; view from the village edge or satellite only, no entry.

name: Rittergut Friedeburg
body:
Large Rittergut manor with a dark, aged roof standing empty above an overgrown park; some neighbouring estate buildings in the village are being re-roofed, but the manor itself appears derelict.

Heritage-listed & private property. ⚠️ Masonry & roof collapse risk.
next: Private, heritage-listed estate in the village; view from the lane or satellite only, no entry.

name: Gutshaus Tornow
status: Derelict manor with tower, wild park
body:
Gutshaus with a small corner tower standing in an overgrown park; the mottled roof is present but deteriorating and the grounds are unmanaged.

Heritage-listed & private property. ⚠️ Masonry & roof decay near the walls.
next: Private, heritage-listed manor; view from the village street or satellite only, no entry.

name: Schloss Dwasieden – Marstall und Pavillons
body:
Neobarocke Villenanlage an der Ostsee: seit der Sprengung 1948 nur Ruinenreste; erhalten sind zwei Pavillons und der 1997 ausgebrannte Marstall. Beliebter Lost Place; 2022 nach Insolvenz an einen Immobilieninvestor verkauft.

⚠️ Absturzgefahr an der Steilküste und durch instabiles Ruinenmauerwerk; Einsturzgefahr (Backstein 1877, kein Asbestschwerpunkt).
next: Privatgrundstück; Betreten ist Hausfriedensbruch – Zutritt nur mit Eigentümererlaubnis.

name: Kindersanatorium Erich Steinfurth
body:
DDR-Kinderkurheim, seit 1991 leer, in OSM als Ruine erfasst. Nach Brandstiftung 2019 schwer geschädigt; unmittelbar südöstlich ein neuer Pflegeheim-Bau (Teil-Neubebauung), das Sanatorium selbst bleibt Ruine.

⚠️ Einsturz- und Brandschäden, offene Decken; Asbestverdacht (Bau vor 1990).
next: Privates, verfallenes Areal; Betreten ist Hausfriedensbruch – nur mit Genehmigung.

name: Kurklinik Stanggaß (ehem. Wehrmacht-Lazarett)
body:
Ehem. Dietrich-Eckart-Krankenhaus (1942), NS-Wehrmachtslazarett, danach Reha-Kurklinik bis 1996; großer mehrflügeliger Bau mit verwittertem, teils offenem Dach, überwuchert – in OSM als Ruine erfasst. Liegt ~450 m ostnordöstlich des ursprünglich genannten Dorfpunkts.

⚠️ Einsturzgefahr, Asbestverdacht (Bau 1942). Umfeld: aktive Klinik Schönsicht (~450 m ONO) und Jägerkaserne (~1 km SW).
next: Privates, verfallenes Klinikareal; Betreten ist Hausfriedensbruch – nur mit Erlaubnis.

name: Siemens-/Charm-Hotel (Resortruine)
body:
Ehem. Siemens-Ferienresort (Adresse Siemensstraße) im Bayerischen Wald mit markantem stern-/sichelförmigem Baukörper; seit 2016 aufgegeben, in OSM als Ruine erfasst.

⚠️ Brandschäden und Verfall, Einsturzgefahr; Bau der 1970er – Asbestverdacht.
next: Abgelegenes Privatgelände; Betreten ist Hausfriedensbruch – nur mit Genehmigung.

name: Rossewitz Manor House
body:
Manor of about 1655–1680, regarded as the oldest Baroque building in Mecklenburg (architect Charles Philippe Dieussart). Roof collapses in 1982 and 1991/92 gutted the interior; the roof has since been rebuilt and the great-hall frescoes conserved, but the house is an empty secured shell and restoration has stalled (flagged again in March 2026).

⚠️ Gutted interior with a history of ceiling and floor collapse; masonry-fall risk. A protected Baudenkmal on private land, supported by a Förderkreis and the Deutsche Stiftung Denkmalschutz.
next: Privately owned and completely closed to the public; arrange access through the owner or the Förderkreis / AG Gutsanlagen advocacy group.

name: Pansevitz Palace Ruin
status: Roofless manor ruin in a public park
body:
The manor (completed 1597) survives only as two roughly 17 m tower ruins and foundation walls, quarried for rubble until about 1999. The landscape park has been restored since 1999 and a steel spiral staircase was placed inside one tower as a viewpoint in 2009. The neighbouring Kavaliershaus is fully renovated and inhabited — that is not the ruin.

⚠️ Unstabilised ~17 m masonry (falling-masonry & collapse risk) and several deep park ponds (open water). A listed Baudenkmal cared for by the Stiftung Schlosspark Pansevitz; the park is also a FriedWald burial forest.
next: The park is publicly walkable and the ruin is foundation-managed; treat the loose masonry with care and respect the burial-forest setting.

name: Dargun Palace and Monastery Ruin
body:
Renaissance palace built onto a former Cistercian abbey and gutted by fire in 1945. Since 1990 it has been secured and rebuilt in stages: the central risalit now holds the town information office and library, and the monastery church nave was reroofed in 2002/03 as a roughly 300-seat hall. Large parts — including the pinned church choir — remain roofless secured ruin.

⚠️ Masonry-fall risk in the unrestored, roofless wall sections. A municipally run heritage complex & venue (guided tours, a local museum, café and the open-air Darguner Musiksommer), so it is a managed ruin rather than an abandoned one.
next: Municipally run and freely accessible in opening hours; the roofless ruin core is walk-in and guided tours are offered, so no urbex entry is needed.

name: Remplin Palace (surviving north wing)
body:
The palace burned down on 10 April 1940; only the north wing survived and was never rebuilt. It sold at auction in 2019 for €18,500 and has since seen only intermittent securing and clean-up, so it remains a derelict shell. A roughly 37 m gate tower of 1750 and the estate church stand nearby.

⚠️ Fire-gutted masonry with collapse risk; asbestos plausible in 20th-century patch repairs. The building is a privately owned Baudenkmal; the surrounding Lenné landscape park is town-owned and nearly restored (2026).
next: The ruin is private and not open; the surrounding park is publicly accessible, so view from there and ask the owner before approaching the building.

name: Ketelshagen Brickworks Ruin
body:
Brickworks founded in 1883; production ended around 1992, leaving an overgrown ring kiln (Ringofen) with its chimney. An investor bought the site in 2014 promising restoration but carried out no work, and sources note it may eventually be demolished as vegetation reclaims the open sheds.

⚠️ Explicitly collapse-prone masonry, asbestos plausible in this pre-1990 industrial site, and standing water. Mapped as historic ruins; a heritage listing is unconfirmed.
next: Private, unsecured and structurally dangerous with no tours; seek the owner’s permission and do not assume any part of the ruin is stable.

name: Ducherow Brickworks Ruin
body:
Brickworks that ceased operating after 1990 and fell into ruin. It is a protected Baudenkmal ensemble — ring kiln (Ringofen), drying chamber, boiler house, rail installation and chimney — with the long kiln building still under a corrugated fibre-cement roof.

⚠️ Likely asbestos-cement roofing (pre-1990 industrial), collapse risk and standing water. Privately owned and unsecured, with no museum or tours.
next: Privately owned, unsecured and heritage-listed; seek the owner’s permission and treat the asbestos roofing and unstable structure as hazards.

name: St.-Lukas-Klinik
body:
Former Catholic hospital in the Ohligser Heide woods, closed on 1 December 2020 and standing empty since. Satellite imagery shows the multi-wing clinic buildings still intact, with no demolition or new construction on the site.

⚠️ Hospital dereliction hazards: likely asbestos, sharps & medical waste, and unsecured floors. An active care home (St. Lukas Pflegeheim) adjoins about 110 m to the west and a row of houses lies to the northeast, so keep well clear of both.
next: The complex sits on private, likely-secured former hospital grounds off Schwanenstrasse deep in the woods; there is no public entry, so any visit would need the owner's permission.

name: St.-Johannes-Hospital
body:
Closed Catholic hospital, tagged as disused in OpenStreetMap and confirmed vacant by a local report of a fire in the empty building. The large multi-wing block still stands with its roof intact.

⚠️ Hospital plus fire-damage hazards: asbestos, sharps & a weakened structure. A school sits only about 90 m to the north and the listed St.-Johannes-Baptist church about 110 m to the southwest, inside a dense residential block.
next: The building stands on private hospital grounds hemmed in by streets, a church and a school; it is not publicly accessible and entry would require the owner's permission.

name: Abandoned industrial complex
body:
Derelict industrial hall at Schwarzbach 133, most likely a former textile (ribbon-weaving) mill and possibly a protected monument. OpenStreetMap classes it as building=ruins, and imagery shows a long hall with a decayed, patchy roof & an empty cracked yard.

⚠️ Ruin hazards: roof and floor collapse plus likely asbestos. It is wedged tight against occupied housing on all sides, so treat resident privacy and any monument protection with care.
next: The ruin is on private land squeezed between occupied houses off Schwarzbach; there is no public access and any entry would need the owner's permission.

name: Domjüch former state asylum
body:
Former Prussian state psychiatric asylum (Landesirrenanstalt Domjüch), opened 1902 by the wooded Domjüchsee; the clinic closed in 1939 and the grounds later saw military use. Eight monument-listed buildings survive as ruins.

Since 2010 a preservation association has stabilised them — roof sealing, chapel restoration — and opens the site seasonally with exhibitions & guided tours. ⚠️ Off the tour paths there are unsecured floors, collapse risk & deep cellars.
next: On association-managed private land; go only on the Förderverein open days or a booked guided tour, not by free roaming.

name: Waldniel-Hostert former hospital (Kent School)
body:
Built 1911 as the Franciscan St. Josefsheim care hospital. Under the Nazi regime a children’s ward here became a site of the murder of disabled patients; the victims’ memorial & cemetery lie about 230 m northwest and are not this pin — please treat that ground with respect.

Post-war it served as a British military hospital (the Kent School), then was abandoned. The mansard-roofed wards now stand empty behind fencing. ⚠️ Asbestos, floor collapse, medical residue & isolation.
next: Private, fenced & monitored ruin — no public access; view from the public lane only and keep well clear of the separate memorial cemetery.

name: Holsthum glassworks ruin
body:
Remains of the Holsthum glassworks, founded 1769; what stands today is the consolidated ruin of the building that once housed the glass melting furnace, in open green ground on the lane Auf der Hütte.

This is a modest heritage remnant — walls & furnace base — not a large explorable structure, and the nearby manor (Schloss Holsthum) is separate, occupied property. ⚠️ Loose masonry & uneven footing.
next: A small open-air ruin on village/private ground — visible on foot; respect the adjoining private gardens and take nothing.

name: Grube Camphausen (Hammerkopfturm)
body:
Hammerkopf winding tower over Schacht IV (1912, 40.7 m) — the oldest surviving pithead tower in German mining and the first ever built in reinforced concrete. The colliery closed in 1990; the yard is now part fallow brownfield, part reused as a Gewerbegebiet (business park).

⚠️ Heritage-listed landmark with concrete spalling; ~40 m fall height if entered; capped shafts & mining subsidence; pre-1990 ancillary buildings (asbestos plausible).
next: Protected monument promoted locally as a landmark; the grounds are externally approachable within the business estate, but the tower interior is not routinely open — ask the Gemeinde Quierschied.

name: Grube Warndt – Förderturm Warndtschacht
status: Heritage tower on a reused site
body:
69.7 m reinforced-concrete winding tower over the Warndtschacht (built 1960–63), heritage-listed; the shaft itself is concrete-filled. Mining ended in 2005/06.

⚠️ Most of the site is actively reused — an operating biomass power plant, a solar array & a metal-recycling yard — so it is a secured, working Gewerbegebiet rather than a free-roam ruin. Pre-1990 buildings (asbestos likely); ~70 m fall height.
next: The heritage tower stands on private, operational commercial ground with an active power plant; not freely walkable — access needs owner permission.

name: Grube Luisenthal – Richardschächte
body:
The listed core survives on a largely cleared pit: the steel headframes of Richardschacht 1 & 2 (1952/1962), their winding-engine houses and shaft halls still stand, while most other buildings were demolished from 2018.

⚠️ Fenced RAG demolition/redevelopment zone becoming a memorial (Ort der Erinnerung) — not freely walkable. Tall headframes; sealed shafts & subsidence; pre-1990 build (asbestos likely). Site of the 1962 disaster (299 dead).
next: RAG-owned, fenced redevelopment site — not open to casual visitors; access would need RAG or municipal permission.

name: Veritas / Nähmaschinenwerk
body:
Vast former Singer/Veritas sewing-machine works — a protected monument whose ~40 production halls have stood largely empty since about 1992. The landmark 49 m clock/water tower is preserved and a power house with two chimneys survives.

⚠️ Parts are reused (a vocational school in the admin block; a firm at the south edge), so the site is fenced/occupied, not free-roam. Pre-1990 build (asbestos plausible); on the busy Berlin–Hamburg line, though internal sidings are disused.
next: Heritage-protected, partly occupied property; the tower is viewable from outside but hall interiors need owner permission.

name: Lokschuppen Rangierbahnhof Wustermark
body:
21-stall Ringlokschuppen with turntable — a heritage ruin (roof partly gone) that has stood unused since DB withdrew, inside the former marshalling yard.

⚠️ It sits within an active rail-tech campus (HVLE workshop, BahnTechnologie Campus, RLCW freight yard) with the live Hannover–Berlin high-speed line (200+ km/h) alongside — serious train/trespass danger. Pre-1990 build (asbestos plausible); a 56 m water tower stands nearby.
next: Fenced, operational railway and commercial-campus land — realistic access only by arrangement with the BahnTechnologie Campus; casual entry is illegal and dangerous.

name: Rundlokschuppen Rummelsburg
body:
Rare circular roundhouse (1879) with a 30 m Schwedler dome and central turntable, heritage-listed and abandoned since 1993 (the 2010 DB demolition bid was rejected) — one of only two of its kind left in Germany. Its only regular use is occasional film shoots.

⚠️ Ringed by live depot tracks inside the working Bahnbetriebswerk Rummelsburg — operational-railway trespass with real train danger. The structure is very marode (collapse risk); pre-1990 build (asbestos plausible).
next: Enclosed by active railway land and hard to reach without crossing live tracks; no legal access — entry means trespassing on an operational depot.

name: Former mother-and-child spa clinic St. Ottilia
body:
OSM names this village-centre building the disused former mother-and-child Kurklinik St. Ottilia. Opened 1995, it has stood empty since a 2004 insolvency; a February 2025 report describes a large complex still awaiting a reuse concept.

⚠️ Long-vacant and decaying, though a post-1990 build means a lower asbestos risk. It lies a few km from the Bavarian Forest national park and close to the Czech border, so drone and airspace limits must be checked.
next: It is an empty building in a public village centre; seek owner permission and check national-park and border-area drone rules before flying.

name: Former Mall-Bräu brewery
body:
The old Fridolin Mall brewery (brewing since 1870) has stood empty for years behind a site fence. OSM tags it an abandoned brewery and local press (August 2025) reports that reuse plans have so far failed.

⚠️ Sealed, deteriorating complex. ⚠️ Probable asbestos in the later 20th-century structures.
next: It is fenced private property in the village; permission from the owner is required and the site is not open to the public.

name: Former Asklepios specialist clinic
body:
OSM tags this three-storey building as an abandoned hospital — the former Asklepios Fachklinik (internal medicine, psychosomatics & psychotherapy). It has stood empty for years and been repeatedly vandalised.

⚠️ Break-ins and decay throughout. ⚠️ As a pre-1990 clinic, asbestos and PCB are likely. This is the Homberg (Ohm) site, not the different town of Homberg/Efze.
next: It is a vacant private clinic on the town edge; seek owner permission and treat the interior as contaminated and unsafe.

name: Malzwerke Gößnitz
body:
A malting works founded in 1889, later the malt plant of VEB Altenburger Brauerei. The main works still stands and is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a ruin; a secondary plant on Uferstraße was already demolished. It is heritage-listed as a “malt works with silo buildings”.

⚠️ The silo and kiln structures carry serious fall and confined-space risk, and roofs are already partly open (collapse hazard); ⚠️ asbestos is likely in this pre-1990 industrial fabric. The complex sits directly beside a live railway.
next: A heritage-listed industrial ruin that is almost certainly fenced and unsafe — seek permission from the owner or town and never enter the silos.

name: Capitol Planitz
body:
A sound-film cinema opened in 1938 with a large auditorium, stage and a 12 m screen, in the tradition of the earlier “Schneiders Lichtspiele”. OpenStreetMap records it as an abandoned cinema ruin, checked as still standing at the end of 2024; it is not heritage-listed.

⚠️ The wide roofed auditorium and stage roof pose a real collapse risk, and the pre-1990 fabric may contain asbestos. It stands on a public street among occupied houses, so expect neighbours and passers-by.
next: An abandoned building on a public street — entering is trespassing and physically dangerous, so photograph from public ground or ask the owner for access.

name: Kammgarnspinnerei Schmelzer
status: Heritage mill, now a business park
body:
A worsted spinning mill built around 1890–1920; production ceased after 1991. It is heritage-listed (Saxony ID 09237761, covering all buildings including the chimney and shed halls). It now functions at least partly as a Gewerbepark (business park), so some units are occupied while derelict wings may remain.

⚠️ Pre-1990 textile-mill fabric means asbestos is plausible, and any empty halls should be treated as structurally uncertain. Because parts are in active commercial use, people and vehicles are present.
next: Heritage-listed and partly an occupied business park — do not treat it as freely abandoned; ask the owner and tenants before entering any part.

name: RENAK-Werke (old Stammwerk)
body:
The published coordinate is the active VCST Reichenbach plant, which is not derelict. The abandoned part is the old RENAK Stammwerk about 500 m ESE at Dammsteinstraße 12: brick industrial halls (1940s) left to decay since 1996, heritage-listed and confirmed still standing in 2025. Part of the grounds is used as a car workshop, and the site was set for forced auction in early 2025, so ownership may be changing.

⚠️ Reported contaminated site (Altlast); ⚠️ pre-1990 asbestos and open, damaged roofs (collapse risk); ⚠️ a live railway runs right along the north side.
next: Derelict but heritage-listed, next to an active car workshop and a working railway — do not enter; seek owner permission and treat the ground as contaminated.

name: Papierfabrik Spechthausen
body:
A former paper mill: production ended in 1956, the site later became a GDR army depot, and after 1990 it was abandoned and decayed. Since 2009 the buildings have been progressively brought back into use, and it is heritage-listed (Denkmal 09175958). Today it is mixed — a residential community project (“Lebensraum Spechthausen”) and small firms occupy parts, while large historic halls south of the road stay derelict.

⚠️ The decaying halls carry collapse risk and pre-1990 asbestos is plausible; ⚠️ the Schwärze stream runs through the site. This is not a free urbex site: parts are inhabited and private.
next: Heritage-listed, private and partly inhabited — obtain permission and respect the residents; only some halls are genuinely empty.

name: Ringofen (brickworks ruin)
body:
The published coordinate 53.02704, 13.29359 is empty former clay-pit land with no building, and the nearby Ziegeleipark is a fenced, staffed museum to avoid. This point is a separate derelict Hoffmann ring-kiln about 2.7 km south (an OpenStreetMap historic ruin): a long brick kiln building at the edge of a flooded pit.

⚠️ It is ringed by deep, cold flooded former clay pits (Tonstiche) — a serious drowning risk; ⚠️ collapse and pre-1990 asbestos are likely, and the site is remote. The northern end may be partly maintained or private.
next: A remote rural ruin reached across private land and water — seek the landowner’s permission, stay well clear of the flooded pit edges, and never enter the museum grounds.

name: Kaufhaus Görlitz (Görlitzer Warenhaus)
body:
Monumental 1913 Jugendstil department store with a glazed central light-court, empty since 2009 and still unrenovated; the owner's partial-demolition request was refused by heritage authorities in 2024.

⚠️ Falling-masonry, ornate-ceiling and roof-collapse risk inside; the building is heritage-listed, sealed and monitored on a busy pedestrian square.
next: Private, heritage-protected and sealed; entry is Hausfriedensbruch and the central pedestrian square makes any approach highly visible.

name: Former Department Store, Mühlenstraße 8
status: Disused store by the Mühlentor gate
body:
Vacant former department store at Mühlenstraße 8 in Grimmen's small historic core, beside the medieval Mühlentor gate.

⚠️ Falling-masonry and roof-collapse risk; a sealed shell in a compact, overlooked town centre.
next: Private and sealed; entry is Hausfriedensbruch and the central location makes any approach conspicuous.

name: Former Filmbühne Cinema
body:
The Filmbühne Malchin cinema at Wargentiner Straße 23, closed in 2020 and now privately owned and disused.

⚠️ Roof-collapse and falling-masonry risk in the auditorium; a sealed building beside the open market green.
next: Private property; entering is Hausfriedensbruch and the open square setting makes it highly visible.

name: Former Odeon Cinema
body:
Former Odeon cinema (dating from 1910) at Dr.-Gebler-Straße 7, disused and embedded in Zeulenroda's dense old-town block.

⚠️ Falling-masonry and roof-collapse risk; sealed and hemmed in by occupied neighbouring houses.
next: Private, sealed and wedged among lived-in houses; entry is Hausfriedensbruch with very high visibility.

name: Former Cinema, Fritz-Schulenburg-Straße
body:
Disused cinema at Fritz-Schulenburg-Straße 21, a low rectangular auditorium hall standing empty in Tangermünde.

⚠️ Roof-collapse and falling-masonry risk; a sealed building among houses and small businesses.
next: Private property; entering is Hausfriedensbruch and the residential street offers little cover.

name: Former St. Josef Church
body:
Small Roman-Catholic diaspora church St. Josef in Löderburg, profaned in 2011 and auctioned in 2012; OSM records it as no longer used.

⚠️ Roof-collapse and falling-masonry risk, plus pigeon-guano (histoplasmosis) hazard inside the sealed nave.
next: Private (auctioned) and sealed on a residential/allotment street; entry is Hausfriedensbruch and readily seen by neighbours.

name: Former Methodist Church
body:
Former Evangelical-Methodist church at Seminarstraße 18; OSM records it as disused (old name only), though one town listing still names the congregation here, so verify locally.

⚠️ Roof-collapse and falling-masonry risk, plus pigeon-guano (histoplasmosis) inside; a sealed building on a residential street.
next: Private and sealed on a built-up residential street; entry is Hausfriedensbruch and highly visible to neighbours.

name: Salzmann-Fabrik
body:
Former Salzmann & Comp. mechanical weaving mill (sailcloth, denim and linen, founded 1891), gutted by a major fire in 1965 and repeatedly hit by arson since. A surviving L-shaped brick monument — a glazed sawtooth shed-hall plus a long two-storey wing — frames a central field of rubble and overgrowth where the burnt-out sections collapsed.

⚠️ Asbestos, fire-ruin collapse and a long arson history. Redevelopment has now begun — Lindhorst's “Wohncarrée Industriedenkmal Salzmann” (~250 flats plus a care home), groundbreaking April 2026 — so the plot is a fenced active construction site and the flyable derelict state is shrinking fast.
next: Now a fenced active construction site around a protected monument; only heritage or press visits by prior permission are legitimate, and casual entry is trespassing and hazardous.

name: Continental-Werk Limmer
body:
The last standing heritage building of the former Continental rubber and tyre works: a long brick hall on the Stichkanal, now largely roofless with its internal bays open to the sky. Almost everything around it has been cleared for the “Wasserstadt Limmer” housing scheme; the nearby ~50 m water tower has been renovated and is not derelict.

⚠️ Contamination in the building fabric (the stated basis for a 2023 demolition order), roofless unstable masonry, construction-site fencing and a canal edge. The hall still stood on 2026 imagery, but demolition has been ordered — verify it survives before relying on this.
next: The canal towpath gives a legal external view; the plot itself is a fenced construction/remediation site, so any closer access is via the developer or heritage bodies only.

name: Berliner Bürgerbräu
status: Derelict listed brewery; part in use
body:
Historic listed Berlin brewery on the Müggelsee/Spree shore; production ceased in March 2010. The pin sits on the large waterfront production hall, its grey roof heavily patched and skylit and still lettered “Berliner Bürgerbräu”, with fermentation silos to the north-west; a renovated building nearby houses a brewery museum and events.

⚠️ Asbestos (pre-2010 industrial), floor and roof collapse, vandal traffic and a water's edge. The heritage complex is still largely empty and vandalised; only the museum and event/biergarten areas are in use.
next: You can legitimately visit the brewery museum and event spaces on part of the grounds; entering the sealed production buildings is Hausfriedensbruch.

name: Kaserne Krampnitz
body:
Former army cavalry/riding school, later Wehrmacht and then Soviet barracks, empty since 1992. A derelict core of long historic barracks with weathered grey roofs survives, but it is shrinking fast as the site is turned into a new district for ~10,400 residents by the early 2030s — cleared plots, active building sites and freshly red-tiled restored blocks now surround it.

⚠️ Asbestos (pre-1990), collapse, and increasingly live construction with heavy machinery, fencing and security. (The given coordinate lay ~1 km south-east on a lakeside weekend-house settlement.)
next: A listed monument with occasional official tours and open days during redevelopment; otherwise it is a hard-fenced construction site and casual entry is trespassing.

name: Olympisches Dorf 1936 / Löwen-Adler-Kaserne
body:
The 1936 Berlin-Olympics athletes' village, later the Löwen-Adler-Kaserne (Wehrmacht, then a Soviet Army sports base). The two rows of original athlete houses are a clear mix — some re-roofed and restored, others with mottled grey roofs, overgrown surrounds and no vehicles; the pin sits on a still-derelict house, with the overgrown historic running track to the north-east.

⚠️ Collapse risk in the unrestored houses and possible asbestos in the later barracks. Since 2017 terraplan has been converting the athlete-house area into housing, so the derelict fragment is steadily shrinking.
next: The restored areas and the still-derelict houses can be visited legitimately on ticketed guided tours, and the Jesse-Owens-Haus is a museum — no trespassing needed for the visitable parts.

name: RAF Hospital Wegberg
body:
Former British military general hospital (RAF Hospital Wegberg, 1953–2010) hidden in woodland near the ex-JHQ Rheindahlen, now German-owned. Its distinctive polygonal ward ring and several ward blocks still stand as roofless, overgrown derelict shells around rubble-strewn courtyards.

⚠️ 1950s-hospital asbestos, structural collapse and — critically — an active phased demolition: newer imagery shows expanding rubble fields where wings have already been razed, so the ruin may be largely gone soon (the pin was on the still-standing polygonal ring on 2026 imagery — re-verify before relying on it). The given coordinate lay ~700 m north-east.
next: Fenced with access barred; it is both a Hausfriedensbruch trespass and a live demolition site, so there is no safe or legitimate entry.

name: Landhaus Bogensee / FDJ-Hochschule “Wilhelm Pieck”
body:
Joseph Goebbels' 1939 country villa “Waldhof am Bogensee” together with the adjoining former GDR youth-leadership college (FDJ-Jugendhochschule “Wilhelm Pieck”), a huge complex empty since 2000. The low L-shaped villa has a moss-dark roof with young trees closing over it and an overgrown courtyard; the multi-storey college blocks stand intact but vacant in the forest.

⚠️ Asbestos in the GDR-era school buildings, unstable floors and collapse risk — a January 2026 fire brought down the main auditorium ceiling; the site is remote forest. Owned by the State of Berlin, with ownership transferring to Wandlitz in 2025 and future use still undecided.
next: The only legitimate way in is a periodic official guided monument tour; unescorted entry is Hausfriedensbruch.

name: Lungenheilstätte Buch (“Stasi-Krankenhaus”)
body:
A grand red-brick H-plan hospital pavilion in the Berlin-Buch hospital forest — the derelict complex urbexers call the “Stasi-Krankenhaus”, though the confirmed identity in the heritage record is Ludwig Hoffmann's former men's lung sanatorium (1901–05); actual MfS/Stasi use could not be verified. Its central and northern wings are roofless and collapsed while the side wings keep red-tile roofs, and the grounds are overgrown.

⚠️ Asbestos (1900s fabric plus GDR refits), roof and floor collapse in the open sections, and an active building site immediately to the north-east. It is part of a listed Ludwig-Hoffmann ensemble as Buch's medical campuses are redeveloped one by one.
next: A protected monument bordered by a live construction site; there is no public access and entry is Hausfriedensbruch.

name: Ringlokschuppen Leipzig-Plagwitz
body:
A derelict brick roundhouse (Ringlokschuppen) in the Leipzig-Plagwitz / Kleinzschocher rail lands, its fan-shaped hall still roofed but visibly decayed, walls heavily graffitied and approach tracks overgrown. The other Leipzig candidate, the Bahnbetriebswerk in Wahren, has lost its roundhouse to demolition, so Plagwitz is the surviving derelict one.

⚠️ Likely asbestos roofing, roof and floor collapse, and nearby live tracks; small businesses use the adjacent yard, so the site is watched.
next: On railway land and private property — entry is Hausfriedensbruch plus railway trespass, and the neighbouring yard is in use, so it is watched.

name: Knappschaftsheilstätte Sülzhayn
status: Roofed ruin; neighbours are open shells
body:
Former miners' (Knappschaft) lung sanatorium in the spa forest above Sülzhayn in the Südharz, built around 1900 and left empty after the spa economy collapsed when the inner-German border cut the village off. German Wikipedia lists it among the site's still-standing ruins — its long wing and entrance pavilion still carry a roof, unlike several neighbours.

⚠️ The sanatoria 15–130 m away in the same forest clearing are roofless shells with collapsed floors, and the whole complex is structurally unstable; assume asbestos in the pre-1990 fabric. No fence is visible on imagery, but the ruins are reached only by unmarked forest tracks.
next: No legal tour exists; entering any of these roof-failing sanatorium shells is Hausfriedensbruch and structurally dangerous.

name: Johanniter-Heilstätte Sorge
body:
Former Johanniter Order tuberculosis sanatorium on the Ochsenberg between Sorge and Hohegeiß, opened in 1902, used as an NVA and later Bundeswehr recreation home from 1968 to 1991 and empty since. German Wikipedia describes strongly advanced decay, with collapsed roof sections over the eastern wing and almost every window broken.

⚠️ Partial roof collapse, unstable floors and likely asbestos in later fittings; the grounds are under a long-term lease (a sled-dog kennel) and were reported fenced, with the informal “Lost Place” visiting scheme ended by 2022. A couple of 2024 blogs still advertise a €5 self-guided visit, which conflicts with the fencing report and should not be relied on.
next: The grounds are leased and reported fenced with public access ended in 2022, so entry is Hausfriedensbruch regardless of older blog claims of a paid self-visit.

name: Diamant-Brauerei
body:
The twin-turreted brewhouse of the Diamant-Brauerei (founded 1841; brewing here ceased in 1994) stands as an industrial ruin — open and holed roofs on the adjoining halls, a roofless shell to the west and an overgrown yard. The pin sits on the brick brewhouse tower block.

⚠️ Collapse risk and probable asbestos-cement roofing (pre-1990 fabric). Immediately alongside, a private micro-brewery has re-brewed in the restored 1841 building since 2006 (not part of this ruin), and since 2025/26 parts of the wider grounds are an active apartment-conversion site (“Diamantwerk”, 176 flats) with cranes and hoarding — so expect people and security nearby; the ruined core still stood on 2026 imagery.
next: Entering the sealed ruin is Hausfriedensbruch and, with a working brewery and an active building site adjacent, discovery is likely; only the restored brewery's museum and events are legitimately visitable.

name: Artillerie-Kaserne Karpin
body:
Part of one of the largest garrisons of the former GDR (NVA 9th Panzer Division, a Bundeswehr site after 1990), given up by the Bundeswehr by 2005 and auctioned off in parcels in 2018/19. The long barracks blocks have stood empty since, with courtyards and access roads reverting to scrub.

⚠️ Collapse risk in the concrete Plattenbau blocks and probable asbestos (GDR-era fabric); parts of the ~120 ha site are now private and may be secured or watched by the new owners, and a solar array and a renovated building occupy separate parcels nearby.
next: The site is private property since the federal auction, so entry is Hausfriedensbruch and may meet owner security.

name: Seeckt-Kaserne (Hohe Wende)
body:
Barracks built 1936–39 for the Wehrmacht, used as the British Army's Trenchard Barracks from 1945 until 2012 and heritage-listed since 1980. Per German Wikipedia the far larger part of the roughly 29 ha ensemble now stands empty and is increasingly decaying; the pin sits on a vacant quadrangle wing with trees growing in its courtyard.

⚠️ Probable asbestos and rotten roof structures (pre-war build). Directly adjoining wings are still in use as refugee accommodation and a municipal works yard (Bauhof) — keep well clear of them; those occupied parts are strictly off-limits.
next: It is federal heritage property, so the legitimate route is prior permission from the property/monument authority; unpermitted entry is Hausfriedensbruch and the occupied wings must not be approached.

name: Porzellanfabrik Schirnding
body:
Former works of Porzellanfabrik Schirnding AG (from 2003 also making the “Arzberg” brand); the roughly 100,000 m² site has stood idle since the 2013 insolvency. Weathered corrugated roofs, no vehicles and vegetation encroaching on the halls are all visible on imagery.

⚠️ Probable asbestos-cement roofing plus kaolin & quartz dust from porcelain production, and collapse-prone hall sections after a decade empty. A 2014 buyer (GPE Passau) planned water-filter/fertiliser production, but imagery shows no new use; the works sit right beside an active railway line.
next: The fenced works are private property beside a live railway, so entering is Hausfriedensbruch as well as physically dangerous.
